papers.title: Non-adjacent triples of cells in a triangular grid: proofs of three conjectured generating functions
papers.abstract: Let $\Tn$ be the triangular grid of side $n$, with its $n^2$ unit cells, and let two cells be side-adjacent if they share an edge and point-adjacent if they share a vertex. We count the orbits of $3$-element sets of pairwise non-adjacent cells under the rotation group $C_3$ and under the full symmetry group $D_3$ of $\Tn$. Three of the four resulting sequences are OEIS A397730, A397731 and A397732, for each of which the only formula on record is a generating function conjectured by Sean A.\ Irvine on 14 July 2026. We prove all three conjectures. The route is Burnside's lemma, together with exact lattice counts for each fixed-point term. The side-adjacency graph turns out to be bipartite, so its triangle count vanishes, and the triangles of the point-adjacency graph have a clean structural description, which gives that count too. Along the way we obtain the first explicit closed forms for the three sequences, each a quasi-polynomial of degree $6$ and period $3$, $6$, $3$ respectively. The same machinery settles the fourth member of the family, whose closed form has been recorded at A289230 without proof since 2017, and the labeled count A289224 that feeds it.

papers.title: Equidistribution of mesh patterns of length 2 on involutions
papers.abstract: We classify all 1024 length-two mesh patterns on involutions into exactly 287 equidis- tribution classes, consisting of 262 trivial classes and 25 nontrivial classes. Since many bi- jections on arbitrary permutations do not preserve the involution condition, our proofs use several involution-preserving bijections, including conjugation and local adjacent-transposition operations, transposition of the RSK recording tableau, prefix-rank swap bijections and marked-occurrence bijections. In particular, we establish the equidistribution of INV-099, a nontrivial class closely related to the unrestricted Class 69, by adapting the marked- occurrence bijection of Zhang and Zhao through a symmetric closure of the marked set. We also obtain explicit distribution formulas and recurrences for several classes, including continued fractions obtained by specializing known labeled Motzkin-path formulas and rational expressions derived from paired skew decompositions of involutions.

papers.title: Estimates for a Parameterized Hankel Functional of Starlike Mappings of Order $\alpha$ and Quasi-Convex Mappings of Type $B$ in Complex Banach Spaces
papers.authors: Sujoy Majumder, Abhijit Banerjee, Shantanu Panja, Debabrata Pramanik
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we introduce and investigate a parameterized Hankel-type functional
  $$H_{2,2}^{\mu}(f)=\mu a_2a_4-a_3^2,\qquad \mu\in[0,1],
  $$ which reduces to the classical second-order Hankel determinant $H_{2,2}(f)$ when $\mu=1$. We obtain estimates for $H_{2,2}^{\mu}(f)$ over the class of starlike mappings of order $\alpha$ on the unit ball of a complex Banach space and on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{U}^n$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$. We also establish estimates for $H_{2,2}^{\mu}(f)$ over the class of quasi-convex mappings of type $B$ on the unit ball of a complex Banach space and on the unit polydisk $\mathbb{U}^n$. For $\mu=1$, our results recover the corresponding estimates for the classical Hankel determinant and extend the known one-dimensional results of Cho et al. \cite{Cho-2018} and Thomas et al. \cite{Thomas-Tuneski} to higher-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Sages and Their Anonymous Slips
papers.abstract: Before the game, the sages agree on a finite set of symbols and on a rule for choosing one of them. They are then seated in an unknown order, either in a row or around a circle with a common clockwise direction. Each sage sees only the adjacent sage or sages and secretly writes one symbol. The slips are then mixed, so nobody learns who wrote which symbol; everyone learns only how many times each symbol occurred. The aim is that every sage should be able to independently reconstruct the entire seating. We ask for the smallest number of distinct symbols that makes this possible. We also consider a version in which the seats have fixed public labels, and each sage is told the label of their own seat. For large numbers of sages, the minimum number of symbols is proportional to the square of the number of sages, up to a constant factor. Several small cases can be settled exactly. Four sages in a row need exactly two symbols, and so do five sages on a circle. Six sages on a circle need exactly three symbols, both with and without labeled seats; we give a short explicit rule. Five sages in a row with labeled seats also need exactly three symbols. Without seat labels, two symbols are impossible, and four are sufficient; whether three symbols suffice remains open.

papers.title: Characteristic Chow Polynomials of Layered-Permutation Intervals
papers.abstract: We study characteristic Chow polynomials of principal intervals in generalized subword order, equivalently of pattern-containment intervals below layered permutations. A terminal-chain recurrence and canonical rightmost embeddings yield a recursive rational generating function for every fixed number of layers, governed by a universal denominator. In the two-layer case we obtain an explicit kernel, prove canonical interlacing when one layer has size at most four, and prove eventual interlacing at every fixed width by a Laguerre limit. We also treat two families with unboundedly many layers. Singleton-prefix intervals have a closed Delannoy-Jacobi gamma polynomial and form real-rooted interlacing sequences. Singleton-sandwich intervals admit rational three-variable series and a marked-slot formula for all gamma coefficients. Their central-layer-two and central-layer-three slices are real-rooted, with interlacing under growth from two to three. For each fixed pair of singleton flanks, a Laguerre differential transform proves eventual interlacing as the central layer grows. These results exhibit composition intervals as a structured testing ground for positivity and root-location questions for Chow polynomials of posets.

papers.title: On the Energy Minimizing Problem in Plasma Dynamics
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in plasma physics and its applications to fusion theory is to find minimum energy stares of plasma.. Hong Qin has suggested the use of what he calls "Gromov ground states" which take into account the phenomenon of symplectic rigidity, as opposed to Gardner's classical approach which only use volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. Howev4er Qin's approach leads to topological difficulties because his constructions remain in the classical (Hamiltonian) domain. We circumvent these difficulties by introducing a quantum-mechanical formulation of the problem, based on the Wigner transform and the symplectic geometry of Gaussian state

papers.title: The minimum number of wheel-saturating edges
papers.abstract:
Let $G$ be an $H$-free graph and $e$ be a non-edge of $G$. We say $e$ is an $H$-saturating edge of $G$, if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. We denote by $f_H(n,m)$ the minimum number of $H$-saturating edges of an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we show that
  $f_{W_{2k+1}}(n,ex(n,F_{2k+1})+1)=
  \begin{cases}
  \ell -k, &(k-2)\ell \ \text{is even},
  2(\ell-k)-1, &(k-2)\ell \ \text{is odd}, \end{cases}$ and $f_{W_{2k}}(n,ex(n,F_{2k})+1)=\left(\frac{2}{33}+o(1)\right)n^2.$
  At the same time, we characterize the corresponding extremal graphs.

papers.title: Nonintersecting Unit Diagonals in Odd Square Arrays
papers.abstract: Let $D(n)$ be the maximum number of unit-square diagonals in an $n\times n$ square array such that no two selected diagonals share an endpoint and no unit square contains both diagonals. We prove that, for every odd positive integer $n$, $D(n)=n(n+1)/2+\lfloor(n+1)/6\rfloor$. The matching lower bound was established by Boyland, Roth, Pint\'er, Lauk\'o, Schoenfield, and Wasielewski. We obtain the upper bound by transforming any admissible selection $M$ in a $(2k-1)\times(2k-1)$ square array into an isometric path cover of the $k\times k$ vertex grid with at most $2k^2-|M|$ paths. An auxiliary matching decomposes the original vertices into alternating paths. On each such path, all segments between blocks are either of type $da$ or of type $bc$. Projecting these paths to the block grid gives coordinate-monotone sequences, which become geodesics when diagonal steps are expanded. The Fisher--Fitzpatrick theorem then yields the sharp upper bound. We also describe a Lean verification of the upper-bound reduction, with the grid-cover theorem supplied as an explicit hypothesis.

papers.title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
papers.abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone. The proof recovers $C(X)$ from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of $L^p$-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.

papers.title: On the minimality of the compact right-angled 120-cell
papers.abstract: We prove that a compact right-angled polytope in hyperbolic 4-space has at least 120 facets, with equality only for the right-angled 120-cell. This answers a question of Potyagailo and Vinberg. As a consequence, the right-angled 120-cell is the unique compact right-angled 4-polytope of minimal volume and f-vector.

papers.title: Second largest eigenvalue thresholds for the vertex-connectivity of regular graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\lambda_2(G)$ and $\kappa(G)$ denote the second largest adjacency eigenvalue and the vertex-connectivity of a graph $G$. For a non-complete $r$-regular graph $G$, Fiedler's inequality $\lambda_2(G)\ge r-\kappa(G)$ shows that $\lambda_2(G)<r-t$ forces $\kappa(G)\ge t+1$. The best such bound is known for $t=1$, by Zhang and Wang, and for $t=2$ with $r\ge4$, by Zhang. In this paper, for every $r\ge3$ and every integer $t$ with $2\le t\le r-1$, we give an upper bound on $\lambda_2(G)$ that forces an $r$-regular graph $G$ to satisfy $\kappa(G)\ge t+1$, and we determine exactly when this bound is best possible. For $\frac{r+2}{2}\le t\le r-1$, Fiedler's bound $r-t$ is already best possible. For $2\le t<\frac{r+2}{2}$, it is replaced by one of two explicit algebraic numbers, and the sign of an explicit polynomial $W(r,t)$, which never vanishes, decides which one applies. Each of the two numbers is attained exactly when $(r,t)$ satisfies an explicit arithmetic condition, and every extremal graph then consists of two cliques and an independent cut of size $t$. In this range our bound also improves a bound of Zhang that holds for every such $t$.

papers.title: Three BMO-type Spaces Characterizing Chord--Arc Curves
papers.abstract: In this note, we introduce three BMO-type spaces on a locally rectifiable Jordan curve and prove that it is a chord-arc curve if and only if these spaces coincide with equivalent norms.

papers.title: Some Expressions involving Bernoulli, Harmonic, and Stirling Numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish several identities involving Bernoulli numbers, harmonic numbers, and Stirling numbers. Our approach extends the method developed by Kargin and Mutluer.

papers.title: Radial reduction, spherical splitting and root counts for two-sided quaternionic polynomials
papers.abstract:
We study quaternionic polynomials whose coefficients may occur on both sides of the variable, using their degree in the four real coordinates. Such polynomials can have no roots, or many more isolated roots than their degree. A simple root has an invertible real derivative, and its sign is the sign of that derivative's determinant.
  For a radial family, the roots over a non-real target reduce to one real equation. We obtain a sharp root bound and follow a change in the signed root count as roots escape to infinity.
  The main results concern spherical root sets for which the polynomial derivative is invertible in the two normal directions. Under a small polynomial perturbation, a sphere splits into simple roots corresponding to the zeros of a tangent vector field, when the derivative of that field is invertible at every zero. We obtain a sharp bound in terms of the perturbation degree and a signed count of two or of minus two.
  For even degrees, the construction yields polynomials with a single leading power and lower-degree terms whose simple root counts, divided by the fourth power of the degree, tend to one as the degree grows. An explicit quartic has 132 simple roots, and this count persists under small coefficient perturbations. For gradient perturbations, the roots correspond to equilibrium directions of an energy on the sphere. This correspondence gives energy thresholds for root disappearance and bounds the critical directions of polynomial orientation profiles in diffusion magnetic resonance imaging.

papers.title: Space curves in Hahn calculus: rotation structure, a fundamental theorem, and $q$-deformed invariants at the fixed point
papers.abstract: We develop the differential geometry of space curves in Hahn's quantum calculus, where the derivative is the difference quotient along the contraction $\sigma(t)=qt+\omega$ with fixed point $\omega_0=\omega/(1-q)$. The Hahn Frenet frame is transported along every orbit of $\sigma$ by rotations through turning and torsion angles, which identifies it with the discrete Frenet frame of the inscribed orbit polygon. An embedded regular Hahn curve is determined, up to linear reparametrization about $\omega_0$, by its trace and the induced contraction. We prove a sharp planarity criterion and a fundamental theorem via an infinite product of rotations and the Jackson--N\"orlund integral. For smooth curves, expansions uniform in $q$ show that at $\omega_0$ the Hahn curvature and torsion carry the factors $[2]_q/2$ and $[3]_q/3$. These factors, a sampling effect of geometrically decaying steps, disappear under edge-length normalization, but their quotient persists in the limiting ratio of torsion and turning angles of every polygon inscribed in a smooth curve with monotonically converging vertices and edge lengths decaying with ratio~$q$. In uniformly sampled relaxation towards a stable node, the factors can become measurable biases. We characterize generalized Hahn helices by a two-step relation between turning and torsion angles; their Lancret ratio at $\omega_0$ is $\pm([2]_q/2)\cot\vartheta$, where $\vartheta$ is the helix angle. Unlike the classical case, a constant ratio of torsion and curvature does not characterize helices: curves with constant curvature and torsion are never generalized Hahn helices, and, near $\omega_0$, unit-speed helices with a given ratio are unique up to similarities and linear reparametrization.

papers.title: A Sharp Distributional Lower Bound for Planar Discrepancy
papers.abstract: We prove that the unnormalized discrepancy function of every $n$-point set in the unit square has absolute value at least $c\sqrt{1+\log n}$ on a set of measure at least $\eta$, with absolute constants $c,\eta>0$. Consequently, its $L_p$-quasinorm is bounded below by $c\,\eta^{1/p} \sqrt{1+\log n}$ for every $p>0$.

papers.title: Non-Induced Representations in Characteristic Zero
papers.abstract: This paper explores the failure of induction from all proper subgroups to generate the full representation ring, measured by a quotient group $Q_k(G)$. We extend existing results for cyclic groups to all finite abelian groups and calculate this quotient for all finite groups over fields of characteristic 0 by reducing to the abelian case. We briefly discuss extensions to positive characteristics via modular representation theory. Finally, we detail our result for certain well-known families of groups.

papers.title: Quantitative Resolvent Calculus for Sample Covariance Matrices
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a quantitative resolvent calculus for sample covariance matrices tailored to applications in high-dimensional statistics. We treat single resolvents, their derivatives, and products of two resolvents with different spectral parameters in the proportional-dimensional regime. Our bounds hold uniformly over compact subsets of $\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R_{\geq0}$ with approximation errors of order $O_{\mathbb P}(\|\Theta_n\|_F/\sqrt n)$ for deterministic test matrices $\Theta_n$. These bounds require only uniformly bounded fourth moments and a uniformly bounded population covariance operator norm. Neither regular spectral edges nor convergence of the population spectral distribution is required. As a key technical ingredient, we develop an averaging argument for centered quadratic forms involving one or two leave-one-out resolvents. Applications of our results include precision-matrix shrinkage, prediction risk in ridge regression, and generalized cross-validation. For these problems, we obtain quantitative guarantees for estimation and data-driven parameter selection.

papers.title: Singular Atiyah Configurations
papers.abstract: We construct arbitrarily large configurations of distinct points in Euclidean three-space with linearly dependent Atiyah polynomials, including planar configurations. The configurations consist of two coaxial cyclic orbits and axial points. We also obtain analogous configurations in hyperbolic three-space.

papers.title: Packaging Systems: Intrinsic Structure, Recovery Ranks, and Globalization Theorems
papers.abstract:
We define packaged structures through carriers, internal units, incidence, candidate spaces, and selected families. A realized packaging system additionally retains a context and formation datum related to its output by a possibly partial, multivalued realization relation. We establish comparison-relative recoverability and non-collapse criteria and an intrinsic refinement-completion theory.
  For atlas specializations, exact extension becomes a specialization-relative packaging completion problem. Under additional recovery and elimination axioms, we establish general globalization sufficiency criteria and sharp classifications for three classes of compatible finite atlases on a fixed cover $\mathcal H$. A geometric obstruction rank $
u(\mathcal H)$ yields thresholds $2k+1<
u(\mathcal H)$ for empty-preserving closures of local Carath'eodory number at most $k\ge1$; $d<
u(\mathcal H)$ for complete functional-dependency theories of local minimum Armstrong size at most $d\ge3$; and $3<
u(\mathcal H)$ for transitive relations, including equivalence relations.
  For nonempty finite label sets and empty-preserving closures, minimum commutant realization dimension equals minimum Armstrong size. We also determine intrinsic recovery ranks and construct canonical clique completions under bounded conformality without chordality. Explicit obstructions establish sharpness; a transport hypothesis is essential for the general recovery--obstruction converse. Complexity bounds apply locally, not necessarily to global extensions.

papers.title: Formalising John Dee's Monas Hieroglyphica in Lean 4
papers.abstract: John Dee's Monas Hieroglyphica (Antwerp, 1564) contains twenty-four numbered theorems about a single composite alchemical glyph, presented in the manner of Euclid: theorem, demonstration, corollary. In this note the following question is considered: which of Dee's theorems can be stated precisely in a proof assistant, and which of them can then be proved? Working in Lean 4 (v4.35.0) with the core library only (without Mathlib), we divide the treatise into three layers: the syntax of the glyph, encoded as inductive data; Dee's arithmetic, verified by kernel computation; and the geometry of the final theorems, in connection with which we prove a classical result not stated by Dee: no ratio of whole numbers doubles the cube, that is, the cube root of two is irrational (the Delian obstruction). The accompanying file Monas.lean compiles with no errors and no sorry. Two observations are made. The cabalistic computation of Theorem XVII, according to which the Cross, "by the best kabbalistic computation," signifies the number 252, is verified, and its proof depends on no axioms: it is a pure computation. The only theorem of the formalisation with genuine mathematical content, the Delian obstruction, is proved constructively and depends only on the axioms propext and Quot.sound.

papers.title: On the unit group of some triquadratic fields
papers.authors: Mohamed Mahmoud Chems-Eddin, Hamza El Mamry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we calculate the unit groups and the $2$-class numbers of the fields $ \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2}, \sqrt{q}, \sqrt{rs})$, where $q\equiv3\pmod4$, $r$ and $s$ are distinct prime numbers satisfying some congruent conditions. As an application of our main results, we derive the precise 2-class number for each field in our family. Furthermore, we show that Greenberg's conjecture is verified for several infinite families of real biquadratic fields.

papers.title: Some new criteria for the uniqueness of limit cycles in Rayleigh--Lienard systems
papers.authors: Hebai Chen, Dongmei Xiao, Rui Zhang
papers.abstract:
In this paper, new uniqueness criteria for
  Rayleigh--Li\'enard systems with damping of positive
  odd degree in the velocity are established.
  Under suitable conditions, any limit cycle is unique
  and hyperbolic, with its stability determined by
  the damping signs.
  Neither symmetry nor monotonicity of the damping
  and restoring functions is required.
  Changes of variables and time yield further criteria
  for generalized Kukles systems.
  Applications to three polynomial families yield
  uniqueness and nonexistence results.
  In particular, we resolve an open uniqueness problem
  for a hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator
  left open by Chen et al. (Phys. D, 2021).
  We also give an alternative uniqueness proof for
  a system with homogeneous components and obtain
  uniqueness and nonexistence results for a modified
  hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator.

papers.title: A new family of deformed trigonometric functions and their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations: application to the nonlinear harmonic oscillator
papers.authors: P. R. Gordoa, A. Pickering, D. Puertas-Centeno, E. V. Toranzo
papers.abstract: In this work we present an extension of the classical trigonometric functions which include, amongst others, the Lindqvist p-trigonometric functions. Additionally, we show their relevance in the study of certain versions of the nonlinear harmonic oscillator equation. Furthermore, we study their more important mathematical properties and obtain their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations. We also define a new extension of the Beta and Ateb sine functions using these new $\chi$-trigonometric functions. Indeed, these new Beta and Ateb functions are involved in the closed form expressions obtained for the solutions of the nonlinear oscillator under certain constraints.

papers.title: Flocking with finite communication speed: a Doppler-inspired Lyapunov approach
papers.abstract: We study the Cucker--Smale model with state-dependent transmission delays arising from finite-speed information propagation. Our main contribution is a Lyapunov functional inspired by the Doppler effect, combining a delay potential with a logarithmic correction involving the receiver velocity. Its dissipation yields uniform delay bounds without relying on velocity contraction estimates. For two agents in one spatial dimension, we prove asymptotic flocking for arbitrary compatible subluminal initial histories, assuming only that the influence function has a divergent integral at infinity. A bounded geometric correction extends this result to arbitrary spatial dimension when all values of the initial velocity histories lie on one common affine line. For multiple agents in one dimension, we obtain uniform delay bounds, and thus flocking, provided that a fixed agent is leftmost for all sufficiently large times. In all these flocking regimes, the spatial diameter remains uniformly bounded and the velocity diameter decays exponentially. We also derive a conditional criterion involving logarithmic sums when the leftmost agent changes infinitely often. Finally, we construct a multidimensional analogue of the Doppler-inspired functional and identify an additional assumption needed to obtain delay bounds in the general case.

papers.title: Variational relaxation and gradient flows for degenerate elliptic conductivity problems
papers.authors: Jan Haskovec, Peter Markowich, Stefano Zampini
papers.abstract: We develop a convex-analytic $L^2$-framework for gradient flows of pumping-energy functionals coupled with elliptic state equations and an evolving nonnegative conductivity $a\geq 0$. The main difficulty is that the conductivity may be merely square-integrable, or degenerate, and formal differentiation need not produce an $L^2$-subgradient. After imposing the strictly positive lower cutoff $r+a\geq r>0$, we define the pumping-energy functional by a variational formula, prove convexity and lower semicontinuity, and show that its $L^2$-subdifferential is nonempty if and only if the pressure gradient belongs to $L^4$. We also obtain a unique maximal-monotone $L^2$-gradient flow satisfying an energy identity. Moreover, we prove Mosco convergence of the pumping-energy functionals as the cutoff vanishes. An inverse-moment conductivity constraint provides a weak alternative to a uniform positive lower bound. For nonlinear laws $a=\mu(b)$, primal and flux representations distinguish two complementary regimes. If $\mu$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional remains convex, and we characterize its $L^2$-subdifferential and the induced gradient flow. If $1/\mu$ is concave, the pumping-energy functional is concave, and therefore its negative is convex. We construct its pointwise gradient flow on a uniformly elliptic box. Admissible stationary points for power laws yield $p$-Laplacian equations with $p>2$ and $1 < p < 2$, respectively.

papers.title: Elmendorf's Theorem for $\infty$-categories
papers.abstract: Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. In particular, we prove that if $G$ is a simplicial group, there is a Quillen equivalence between the homotopy category of $\infty$-categories with $G$-action and the homotopy category of $\infty$-category-valued presheaves on the orbit category of $G$. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.

papers.title: Extremal cosine sign correlations
papers.authors: Shengyang Zang, Yingyu Zhao, Yunhao Zhao, Chen Zhou
papers.abstract: We prove that four cosines with distinct positive integer frequencies have the same sign on at least $1/33$ of a period, with equality precisely for positive integer dilates of $\{1,3,11,33\}$. If both odd and even frequencies occur, the optimal proportion is $1/24$; equality holds precisely for odd positive integer dilates of $\{1,3,4,12\}$ and $\{2,4,5,15\}$. For arbitrary $n$, we establish the universal lower bound $4^{1-n}$ and construct frequency sets for which this proportion is at most $16n^\theta4^{-n}$, where $\theta=\log_2(3/2)$. These bounds determine the optimal exponential decay rate $1/4$.

papers.title: Extensions of a family of Linear Cycle Sets whose underlying group is a product of two cyclic groups
papers.authors: Jorge Guccione, Juan Jos\'e Guccione, Christian Valqui
papers.abstract: We use the linear cycle set cohomology in order to compute extensions of a non trivial linear cycle sets whose underlying additive group is a product of two cyclic groups.

papers.title: Cutoff profile for the coupon collector with many collections
papers.abstract: We solve the problem posed by Erd\H{o}s and R\'enyi in $1961$ about the limiting distribution of the number of draws $T_{n,m}$ that a coupon collector needs to complete $m$ collections of $n$ distinct types of coupons, when $m$ increases with $n$. For fixed $m$, Erd\H{o}s and R\'enyi proved that $\mathbb P(T_{n,m}\leq n\log n+(m-1)n\log\log n-n\log (m-1)!+\theta n)$ converges to $ \mathcal G(\theta)$, for every $\theta \in \mathbb R$, as $n \to \infty$, where $\mathcal G$ is the standard Gumbel distribution function, and they asked what happens when $m=m(n)$ increases with $n$. We give a complete answer to this question. More precisely, for every increasing sequence $m=m(n)$, we determine explicit sequences $t_{n,m}$ and $w_{n,m}$ satisfying $w_{n,m}/t_{n,m}\to0$ such that $\mathbb P(T_{n,m}\leq t_{n,m}+\theta w_{n,m})\to\mathcal G(\theta)$ for every $\theta\in\mathbb R$. We also determine the corresponding asymptotic behavior of $\mathbb E[T_{n,m}]$. To prove these results, we present a methodology, inspired by Poissonization, that can be applied to determine the asymptotic behaviors of standardized hitting times of discrete-time stochastic processes.

papers.title: Derivative-Informed Dimension Reduction of Stochastic Differential Equations: A Path-Space Sensitivity Approach
papers.authors: Joanna Zou, Han Cheng Lie, Youssef Marzouk
papers.abstract: Uncertainty in the drift of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) induces uncertainty in statistical observables defined as expected functionals on path space. We propose a derivative-informed method for identifying low-dimensional structure in the drift-to-observable map, with the aim of improving the tractability of uncertainty quantification. This approach can be viewed as a generalization of the active subspace method to infinite-dimensional input spaces and to path-space observables of SDEs. Representing uncertainty in the drift by random perturbations in a Hilbert space, we construct a path-space sensitivity operator using first-order Fr\'echet derivatives of the observable with respect to the perturbation. We establish conditions under which the leading eigenfunctions of this operator correspond to directions of maximum mean squared sensitivity of the observable, thus enabling low-dimensional approximation with certified error bounds. We further introduce a martingale control variate of the Fr\'echet derivative that reduces error in sample-based estimators of the operator. Using a Galerkin scheme for numerical discretization, we show that reduced representations of the drift from the derivative-informed basis yield more accurate approximations of mean first hitting times of SDEs than the Karhunen-Lo\`eve expansion of the same truncation order.

papers.title: Dynamics of two-dimensional Bose gases in the focusing case
papers.abstract: We prove the propagation of Bose--Einstein condensation and a norm approximation for the dynamics of a Bose gas with localized initial data in two dimensions with singular interactions that may have a small attractive part. We allow the scaling of the interaction to be any polynomial scaling $N^\beta$ for $0<\beta<\infty$ and even exponential scaling $e^{N^\kappa}$ for $0<\kappa<1/4$. Our approach covers external potentials that are time-dependent, at most quadratic, and bounded below, including the situation without an external potential.

papers.title: $L^\infty$ blow-up in the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
papers.abstract:
We investigate the fourth-order Jordan-Moore-Gibson-Thompson equation
  \bee
  u_{tttt}+\al u_{ttt}+\bet u_{tt}-\gamma \Del u_{tt}-\del \Del u_{t}-\varrho \Del u=(f(u))_{ttt}+(f(u))_{tt}
  \eee 
  under homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions in a smooth bounded domain $\Om \subset \R^n$ with $n\leq 3$, where
  $\al \in \R$ and $\bet,\gamma,\del,\varrho>0$. First, for any suitably regular initial data and assuming that $f\in C^4(\R)$ with $f(0)=0$, we prove that the corresponding initial-boundary value problem admits a unique maximal strong solution $u$ on $(0, \tm)$.
  Second, by combining three time-integrated formulations with a series of resolvent-regularized energy estimates, we show that gradient blow-up is ruled out in the sense that
  \be{EE}
  \tm<\infty \quad\,\, \Rightarrow\quad\,\, \limsup_{t\nearrow \tm}\|u(\cd,t)\|_{L^{\infty}(\Om)}=\infty. \tag{$\star$}
  \ee 
  Finally, assuming in addition that $f$ is convex and grows superlinearly in the sense that
  \bee
  f''(\xi)\geq 0 \;\; \mbox{ for all}\;\;\xi \in\R, \qquad \frac{f(\xi)}{\xi}\rightarrow +\infty\;\;\mbox{ as}\;\; \xi\rightarrow +\infty , \qquad \int_{\xi_{0}}^{\infty}\frac{d\xi}{f(\xi)}<\infty \;\; \mbox{ for some}\;\; \xi_{0}>0,
  \eee
  we employ the extensibility criterion (\ref{EE}) to prove that, for a suitable class of initial data, the solution blows up in finite time in the $L^\infty$-norm. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first rigorous description of finite-time blow-up for a genuinely nonlinear equation of fourth order in time.

papers.title: Absorption probabilities of random walks without symmetry or general position
papers.abstract: Let $S_1,S_2,\dots$ be a random walk in $\mathbb R^d$ with independent identically distributed increments. We show that, for every distribution of the increments and for every $n\ge1$, \[ \mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S_1,\dots,S_n)\bigr] = \sum_{m=1}^n\frac1{m!}\sum_{\substack{k_1,\dots,k_m\ge1\\ k_1+\dots+k_m=n}}\frac{1}{k_1\cdots k_m}\,\mathbb P\bigl[0\notin\mathrm{conv}(S^{(1)}_{k_1},\dots,S^{(m)}_{k_m})\bigr], \] where $S^{(1)},S^{(2)},\dots$ are independent copies of the walk. No symmetry, general position or moment assumptions are needed. The result rests on a deterministic identity: for arbitrary vectors $x_1,\dots,x_n$, the number of orderings for which the convex hull of the partial sums avoids the origin equals the number of permutations for which the convex hull of the cycle sums avoids it. We derive it from a permutation-averaging identity for valuations obtained in our earlier work. Consequences include the identities of Sparre Andersen and Spitzer, the distribution-free absorption probabilities of Kabluchko, Vysotsky and Zaporozhets, their generating function found by Petrov, Randon-Furling and Zaporozhets, and a formula for the probability that the origin is never absorbed.

papers.title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{\mu_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_\sigma(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(\mu_k)\to\beta(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists.

papers.title: Explicit strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs using a new graph parameter
papers.abstract: A strong blocking set is a set of points in a finite projective space that intersects every hyperplane of the space in a spanning set of the hyperplane. These objects have been studied both in finite geometry and coding theory due to their equivalence with minimal codes. We give an explicit construction of strong blocking sets using expander graphs that improves the explicit construction of Alon et al. (Noga Alon, Anurag Bishnoi, Shagnik Das, Alessandro Neri, Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society ) by introducing a new geometrically motivated graph parameter that is better suited for this problem. Using this approach, we improve the constant $C$ in the explicit construction of a strong blocking set of size $C (q+1) k$ in the $(k - 1)$-dimensional projective space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q \geq 7$.

papers.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
papers.authors: Cathy Cheng, Nigel Higson, Danilo Polo Ojito, Emil Prodan
papers.abstract: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.

papers.title: Some remarks on polynomial vector fields in $\RR^2$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study planar polynomial vector fields admitting invariant circles. We characterize polynomial vector fields having $m$ concentric invariant circles, and we describe those having three invariant circles whose centers are not collinear. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for the unit circle to be the unique limit cycle of a quadratic vector field. We prove that a cubic or quartic Kolmogorov vector field having the unit circle invariant has no circular limit cycle, and that a quartic vector field with two concentric circular limit cycles has at most three circular limit cycles, this bound being sharp.

papers.title: On the stability of rank-one factors for Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions
papers.abstract: We prove $C^1$-stability of $C^\infty$ rank-one factors for a large class of higher rank Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions. If the factor is a projection of a smooth fiber bundle and the action contains an element which acts as the identity on the rank-one factor and is Anosov on every fiber, then any sufficiently $C^1$-small $C^\infty$ perturbation of the action will also have a $C^\infty$ rank-one factor. In particular, we prove the $C^1$-stability of the product structure for Anosov $\mathbb Z^2$-actions which are obtained as a (diagonal) product of two $\mathbb Z$-Anosov actions.

papers.title: Partial Airy ideals and coloured blobbed topological recursion
papers.authors: Ga\"etan Borot, Vincent Bouchard, Swagata S. Datta
papers.abstract: We define and study the notion of partial Airy ideals, which are certain linear systems of PDEs that may contain less equations than variables. We show that they admit a unique solution of exponential type (the partition function) modulo a choice of initial condition. We construct a large class of examples of partial Airy ideals attached to spectral curves using twisted free-field representations of $\mathcal{W}(\mathfrak{gl}_r)$-algebras at self-dual level. This generalizes the results of Bouchard- Borot-Chidambaram-Creutzig-Noshchenko by significantly enlarging the set of admissible spectral curves, provided they come with additional data that we call colour. We show that the differential constraints on the partition function are equivalent to a set of equations on the associated correlators, which we call coloured loop equations. We find a recursive residue formulation for the solutions of those equations, the coloured blobbed topological recursion}, which is a generalization of the currently known forms of topological recursion. It includes the blobbed topological recursion of Borot-Shadrin as a special case, giving it a natural interpretation within the formalism of partial Airy ideals.

papers.title: Two parametric $q$-supercongruences from Andrews' multi-series transformation
A non-equilibrium thermodynamics formulation of shear set-points in adaptively remodeling vascular networks
papers.abstract:
Blood vessels remodel in response to wall shear stress while the network operates
  under a metabolic maintenance budget. For a power-law maintenance cost, minimizing
  dissipation at fixed budget yields a local shear set-point, and a purely local adaptation rule
  drives the network towards this optimum. Here we give this result a non-equilibrium thermodynamic
  formulation. Blood flow is an exactly linear Onsager system, and the slow remodeling of vessel radii
  is a gradient flow generated by a Rayleigh dissipation functional. This identifies the structural
  mobility, which scales inversely with the maintenance cost of each vessel and can be measured from
  radius fluctuations. Enforcing the budget exactly requires a time-dependent metabolic multiplier,
  which we obtain in closed form; with a fixed multiplier the budget is violated by up to one third
  during transients. The fluid displaced by remodeling vessels couples flow and structure through a
  symmetric, non-diagonal mobility, so that Onsager reciprocity becomes a testable statement:
  neighbouring vessels should show anticorrelated radius fluctuations. With noise, the structural
  sector obeys a second law and an integral fluctuation theorem. Non-reciprocal signaling between
  vessels, such as upstream conducted responses, then breaks the time-reversal
  symmetry of radius fluctuations and produces housekeeping entropy, detectable from time series of
  realistic length. Finally, we construct a partition function over network
  topologies with the number of loops as order parameter. Numerical tests show that loop counts do
  not collapse onto a single curve against an effective temperature, and that they
  depend strongly on the detection threshold.

papers.title: Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin methods for the Keller-Segel model
papers.authors: Silvia Bertoluzza, Gabriella Bretti, Micol Pennacchio, Christophe Prud'homme
papers.abstract: We propose a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) finite element method to approximate the solution of the time-dependent Keller-Segel model, a drift-diffusion system describing chemotactic cell movement. We develop and analyze the corresponding HDG scheme, and establish theoretical convergence results for the proposed discretization. Finally, we present numerical experiments that confirm the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a sphere other than the 4-sphere is regular. On even-dimensional spheres other than the 4-sphere we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics of non-constant curvature carrying Besse families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism.

papers.title: Localized Hybrid Analytical-Finite-Element Thermal Modeling for Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.authors: Mohammad Amin Mohammadi Golafshani, Krishnan Suresh
papers.abstract: Hybrid analytical--finite-element methods support scan-resolved, part-scale thermal simulation of laser powder bed fusion, but their analytical evaluation cost grows as scan-line contributions accumulate. This work develops a space--time localized hybrid formulation that restricts where and how long each contribution is evaluated analytically. Residual terms and boundary conditions derived from the heat equation allow the finite-element correction to account for the thermal effect of contributions removed from the analytical field. The formulation is assessed using a single-line benchmark against an independent full finite-element solution and multiline comparisons with the conventional hybrid formulation. Localization limits the number of analytical contributions retained while maintaining close agreement with the conventional solution. A comparison with uncompensated temporal truncation demonstrates the importance of the residual correction in retaining the thermal effect of removed contributions. In the 500-line case, analytical and total simulation times are reduced by factors of approximately 25.5 and 3.92, respectively, with a relative nodal 2-norm difference of 0.139%.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on Continuous Treatment Effects under Unobserved Confounding
papers.abstract: We study partial identification of conditional treatment effects with a continuous treatment under unobserved confounding. We target the conditional average potential outcome (CAPO) E[Y_x|z] and the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) between two treatment levels. We assume a bounded outcome and Lipschitz continuity of the response functions and of the propensity scores given the latent confounder, and show that these conditions imply the smooth treatment response and smooth treatment selection conditions of Kim et al. (2018). The combined bound of Kim et al. uses only two reference points on the identified diagonal and is generally loose. Bounding through every diagonal reference point instead gives explicit bounds whose average is the sharp identified set of the CAPO at every treatment, inside or outside the observational support. Capping the difference between the upper and lower bounds gives sharp causal bounds on the CATE. These bounds are informative without monotonicity or overlap assumptions.

papers.title: On the Upsilon invariant and the Baldwin-Vela-Vick b-invariant of fibered knots
papers.abstract: For a null-homologous fibered knot $K$ in a rational homology sphere, Baldwin and Vela-Vick define a refinement $b(K)$ of the Ozsv\'ath-Szab\'o contact invariant. We prove that if the Ozsv\'ath-Stipsicz-Szab\'o concordance invariant Upsilon has slope $\Upsilon'_K(t)=-g(K)$ for some $t\in[0,\frac{2}{n+1})$, where $g(K)$ is the genus of $K$, then $b(K)>n$. This extends a result of He, Hubbard, and the author on the Upsilon invariant and right-veering monodromies. We also prove that the knot Floer homology of a fibered knot in the $g(K)-b(K)$ Alexander grading is nonvanishing. As an application, we give many families of fibered cable knots whose $b(K)$ invariant grows arbitrarily large. Finally, we prove that if a monodromy of a fibered knot is neither right-veering nor left-veering, then the third-to-top term of knot Floer homology is nonvanishing.

papers.title: Minimum orders of clique oddomorphism counterexamples
papers.abstract: An oddomorphism to $K_n$ is a proper colouring with $n$ colours in which every vertex is designated odd or even, every vertex has in each other colour class a number of neighbours of its own parity, and every colour class contains an odd number of odd vertices. We prove that an oddomorphism witness to $K_n$ on at most $n+6$ vertices contains a $K_n$ minor with every branch meeting the witness's specified odd set. The conclusion holds inside any graph containing the witness and therefore applies to weak oddomorphisms. The bound is sharp: for every $n\ge8$ the minimum order of a graph admitting a weak oddomorphism to $K_n$ but having no $K_n$ minor is exactly $n+7$. The extremal example is a fifteen-vertex graph with an oddomorphism to $K_8$, obtained from the doubled theta graph of Kriesell and Mohr by adding one vertex adjacent to the seven roots; we give a structural proof that it has no $K_8$ minor, including their counting argument for the rooted case. A separate technical companion records further results on related root-apex graphs, an attachment theorem and a bounded nine-colour statement, together with their computational provenance; none of it is used here. The results do not resolve the unrestricted clique-target problem.

papers.title: Weak type $(1,1)$ estimates for noncommutative maximal truncated rough singular integrals
papers.abstract: We prove a weak type $(1,1)$ estimate for maximal truncations of noncommutative rough singular integrals whose angular kernels satisfy the classical $L\log L$ integrability and cancellation conditions. The main ingredient of the proof is a new linearization method for handling the maximal truncations acting on the bad functions arising from the noncommutative Calder\'on--Zygmund decomposition.

papers.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
papers.abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.

papers.title: On the transformation of unbounded convergent sequences by linear operators on Banach lattices
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a weak variant of the concept of unbounded Dunford-Pettis linear operators, which we call unbounded weak Dunford-Pettis operators. We investigate the properties of this new class, establish inclusion and coincidence results involving unbounded Dunford-Pettis operators, and examine its relationship with the class of unbounded absolutely weakly continuous operators.

papers.title: On the evenness of coefficients of modular forms
papers.abstract: We study the density of primes such that $a_p$ is divisible by a prime above $2$ for modular forms $f = \sum_{n \ge 1} a_n q^n$ of small levels. First, we reduce the problem to low weight and odd level, or a mod $2$ CM type form. Then, we provide calculations for the evenness of particular newforms. In particular, we provide a list of levels where this "evenness" can be computed exactly for all the forms with trivial nebentypus.

papers.title: Blind Random Search with Noisy Measurements: Almost Sure Convergence and Convergence Rates
papers.abstract: Blind random search is a simple global optimization method that only requires the value of the loss function, without needing gradient information or an explicit loss model. However, its classical formulation assumes that the loss evaluation is noise-free, which limits its direct application to practical problems with noisy measurements. We extend blind random search by combining a vanishing acceptance threshold with the running average of noisy loss measurements. Under the stated assumptions, we prove that the proposed algorithm converges almost surely to the global minimizer. We further analyze the rate at which the loss at the current estimate approaches the minimum loss. For low-dimensional cases, we obtain an almost sure asymptotic upper bound on the difference between the two, and for high-dimensional cases, we prove that this difference, suitably scaled, has an exact Weibull limiting distribution.

papers.title: Congruence lattices of $2$-valued unary algebras
papers.authors: Mikl\'os Dorm\'an, Kamilla K\'atai-Urb\'an, Eszter K. Horv\'ath, Tam\'as Waldhauser
papers.abstract: We study congruence lattices of finite algebras whose basic operations are unary and have exactly two values. We prove that the class of finite lattices representable in this way is closed under taking filters, glued sums and ordinal sums, and direct products with finite distributive lattices, but it is not closed under taking ideals or arbitrary direct products. A classification of lattices with at most seven elements with respect to representability is also presented.

papers.title: A crystallographic quotient of the framed braid group and associated flat manifolds
papers.authors: \^Enio Leite, Oscar Ocampo, Paulo Cesar Cerqueira dos Santos J\'unior, Ana Carolina Moura Teixeira
papers.abstract: We study the quotient of the framed braid group $FB_n$ by the commutator subgroup of the framed pure braid group $FP_n$. We prove that $$ \frac{FB_n}{[FP_n,FP_n]}\cong\mathbb Z^n\rtimes\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}, $$ and, for $n\geq3$, that this quotient is a crystallographic group of dimension $n(n+1)/2$ with holonomy group $S_n$. We investigate its finite-order elements and conjugacy classes, prove that it has no elements of finite even order, and construct Bieberbach subgroups with prescribed finite $2$-group holonomy. Starting from suitable Bieberbach subgroups of $\frac{B_n}{[P_n,P_n]}$, we then construct Bieberbach subgroups of the framed quotient whose associated compact flat manifolds are torus bundles over the corresponding unframed flat manifolds. We describe these bundles through the generalized Calabi construction and determine their orientability, first Betti numbers, and the centers of their fundamental groups. As an application, we study a family with cyclic holonomy of odd order, obtaining a criterion for the existence of flat K\"ahler structures, and indicate how the same construction applies to cyclic holonomy of $2$-power order.

papers.title: Intermediate subalgebras of cross-product von Neumann algebras arising from weakly compact actions
papers.abstract: In this short paper, we establish the following Galois-type property for all measure-preserving, weakly compact actions $G \curvearrowright (X,\mu) $ of a non-inner amenable group $G$ on a standard probability space $X$: for any intermediate von Neumann subalgebra $\mathcal L(G)\subseteq \mathcal N \subseteq L^\infty (X)\rtimes G$, there is a factor $G\curvearrowright Y$ of $G \curvearrowright X$ such that $\mathcal N= L^\infty(Y)\rtimes G$. In particular, this holds for all pmp distal actions $G\curvearrowright X$, thereby answering positively an open problem from \cite{BCCMSW24} (which can also be traced back to \cite{CD20}). We also provide an example showing our result is optimal.

papers.title: Statistical inference for boundary constrained parameters
papers.authors: Jaeseon Lee, Anirban Bhattacharya, Suhasini Subba Rao
papers.abstract: Estimation and inference under boundary constraints arises in many areas of statistics, but the available asymptotic theory remains limited and fragmented relative to the classical case, where the parameter lies in the interior of the parameter space. In this paper we derive a boundary-constrained analogue of the standard asymptotic expansion for a minimiser of a loss function, in which the deviation of the estimator from the population parameter is decomposed over lower-dimensional subspaces determined by the directional derivatives at the minimiser. Using this decomposition we show that the limiting distribution of the estimator is a mixture of point masses and truncated skew-normal distributions, with mixture probabilities determined by the directional derivative conditions. A consequence of this result is that the constrained and unconstrained coordinates do not separate: the presence of parameters on or near the boundary affects the sampling distribution of the unconstrained parameter estimators. We apply the expansion to obtain the asymptotic distribution of the quasi log-likelihood ratio statistic under a range of null hypotheses, and since the resulting mixture is not pivotal in the quasi-likelihood setting, we propose a simulation-based procedure for approximating critical values. The framework unifies and simplifies several existing results. We illustrate the methodology by testing for interactions in exponential family graphical models, where the parameters are subject to compatibility constraints that ensure a joint distribution exists.

papers.title: A proof of Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture. A D-coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring in which every subgraph isomorphic to $K_4$ minus an edge is rainbow. Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ has a D-coloring with 9 colors if $\Delta=4$, 10 colors if $\Delta=5$, and $2\Delta-1$ colors if $\Delta\ge 6$. Hu, Kong and Wang proved the cases $\Delta\le 5$ and $\Delta\ge 33$. We prove the sharp bound $2\Delta-1$ for every $\Delta\ge 6$, settling the remaining cases. The proof uses discharging; the case $\Delta=6$ is computer-assisted.

papers.title: Consistency in fractional Korn's inequalities on Lipschitz domains
papers.abstract: We investigate fractional analogs of Korn's inequality on bounded Lipschitz domains in several contexts. Constrained and unconstrained inequalities are established; constraints include quotient spaces and spaces incorporating various classes of boundary conditions or volume constraints. We also expand the parameters of integrability for which the inequalities hold. Specifically, a fractional Korn's first unconstrained inequality holds for vector fields in the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ for all $p \in [1,\infty]$ and all $s \in (0,1)$. In the cases $p = 1$ and $p = \infty$, the inequality has no local analog. We quantify this by investigating the consistency of the inequalities as the differentiability parameter $s \to 1$; the universal constant in the inequality remains stable for $p \in (1,\infty)$ but degenerates for $p \in \{1,\infty\}$. We introduce an explicit $L^p$-bounded projection operator onto infinitesimal rigid motions as a key tool to quantitatively strengthen the inequality.

papers.title: Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their stability directly without assuming LLC, and proved the stability of the depth-$r$ projectors. Following the idea, the first author and Tsao-Hsien Chen produced a family of elements in the center which are conjecturally stable using Deligne-Lusztig parameters attached to irreducible representations. This paper proves the stability of the projectors corresponding to strongly regular Deligne-Lusztig parameters in depth-zero, and for all the positive depth elements with some restrictions on the residue characteristic.

papers.title: The Intersection of nested filled-in little Julia sets have zero area
papers.abstract: It is shown that for any infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial $Q_c$ the intersection $K_\infty$ of all the little filled-in Julia sets (renormalization Julia sets) containing the critical value have zero area.

papers.title: First-order Methods for Variational Inequality Problems with Semi-Infinite Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper studies first-order methods for monotone variational inequalities with semi-infinite constraints and presents this model as a framework covering constrained saddle-point problems, robust optimization, distributionally robust function-constrained optimization, and generalized Nash equilibrium formulations. Since feasibility must hold over infinitely many indexed constraints, direct projection onto the full feasible region is generally difficult. Therefore, we propose a single-loop primal-dual constraint extrapolation method (PD-ConEx) that updates primal variables, Lagrange multipliers, and worst-case constraint indices using first-order information, linearization, extrapolation, and projections only onto simple sets. We establish convergence guarantees for smooth and nonsmooth regimes, showing how the achievable rates depend on strong monotonicity and strong concavity of the index block. For coupled convex-concave saddle-point problems, strong convexity in the minimization block can accelerate its smooth terms even without strong concavity in the maximization block. We also develop an adaptive smooth variant with $O(1/K)$ VI-gap and feasibility guarantees without an a priori bound on generated multipliers. Moment-based and Wasserstein distributionally robust models fit within the framework, and numerical experiments on robust quadratic instances and distributionally robust learning illustrate the method's optimality and feasibility behavior.

papers.title: When Are Nesterov Trajectories Eventually Locally Minimizing?
papers.abstract: We revisit the variational characterization of Nesterov's celebrated method and study when Nesterov trajectories are eventually locally minimizing in a variational sense, a notion that we define precisely. We show that this question is equivalent to the nonnegativity of an associated Schr\"odinger operator acting on variations of the trajectory. For power objectives of the form \[ f(x)=\frac{1}{p}\|x\|^p \] (where $\| \cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm), we give a complete characterization: Among all exponents $p\ge 2$, the Nesterov trajectory with non-zero initial position is eventually locally minimizing if and only if $p=4$. We further interpret this exceptional exponent through the stability theory of semilinear elliptic equations.

papers.title: Berry-Esseen bounds for products of random matrices under a $2+\delta$ polynomial moment
papers.authors: Zhi-Jun Cai, Qi-Man Shao, Hui Xiao, Zhuo-Song Zhang
papers.abstract: Let $(g_{k})_{k \geq 1}$ be a sequence of independent and identically distributed matrices with law $\mu$ on $\mathrm{GL}(d,\mathbb{R})$, where $d\geq2$ is an integer. Suppose that the closed semigroup generated by the support of $\mu$ is strongly irreducible and proximal and that the polynomial moment of order $2+\delta$ is finite, where $0<\delta\leq 1$. We establish a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-\delta/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1} v\|$, where $v$ is a nonzero vector in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is an arbitrary norm on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$. As an application, we also obtain a Berry-Esseen bound of order $n^{-\delta/2}$ for $\log \| g_{n} \cdots g_{1}\|$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is any matrix norm. The proof combines an $m$-dependent approximation with Stein's method. The argument uses identities for exchangeable pairs constructed by resampling individual matrices, together with a concentration inequality for sums of the approximating variables.

papers.title: The Number of Polytope Trees and Beyond
papers.abstract: We study the symmetry-weighted enumeration of complexes formed by gluing copies of a regular polytope. For polytope trees and complexes obtained by attaching such trees to a fixed initial complex, we derive cut-and-join recurrences, differential equations for generating functions, explicit counting formulas, and asymptotic estimates. We then extend the method to complexes with cycles in their dual graphs, enumerating them by the numbers of polytopes and free facets. We derive recurrence relations and partial differential equations for the corresponding bivariate generating functions. In this setting, we obtain recurrences for connected configurations and explicit coefficient formulas for possibly disconnected configurations, both with and without a distinguished initial complex.

papers.title: Optimal Non-Homogeneous Improvements of the Anisotropic Hardy Inequality
papers.authors: Giuseppina di Blasio, Giovanni Pisante, Georgios Psaradakis
papers.abstract: We consider the Hardy inequality associated with a strongly convex Finsler norm $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and we study its optimal non-homogeneous improvements in the whole range $1<p<\infty$. We show that the anisotropic Hardy difference controls a weighted critical Sobolev norm when $1<p<n$, a weighted exponential integrability of Trudinger type when $p=n$, where the Hardy term is replaced by its Leray logarithmic correction, and a weighted H\"older seminorm when $p>n$, proving in each regime that the logarithmic weights appear with the optimal exponents. In the borderline case $p=n$ this extends to general functions the optimal exponent previously known only for anisotropically radial functions. The proofs rely on a common ground-state reduction, combined with a splitting into an $F_o$-radial and a mean-free part for $1<p\le n$, and with an anisotropic Morrey representation formula for $p>n$.

papers.title: Protect the Decision, Not the Disaster: Regret-Robust Capacity Sizing and Positioning with Transportation Recourse
papers.abstract: An operator who positions mobile resources before a disruption faces two uncertainties that are usually treated as one: how the joint state of demand and travel conditions will vary, and which part of the resulting cost the positioning decision can actually change. Standard distributionally robust optimization (DRO) protects total cost, and therefore spends much of its protection on disruption costs that every feasible design would pay. This paper evaluates the worst-case regret of a design and compares it with the worst-case premium of total-cost DRO, and shows that the regret-to-premium ratio can be bounded before any robust model is solved: from marginals for the dependence question, and from single-scenario optima and one transport linear program for the regret question. The worst-case law is a relabelling of the operating record, reassigning every recorded period wholesale to another recorded period, except at most one, which is split. The comparator that exposes the largest worst-case regret is found by a single mixed-integer program. We derive an explicit radius where the sample-average design is exactly regret-robust. For finite scenario and design sets we compute a design's worst-case regret exactly, bound it from quantities a planner already has, and show on fleet and EMS data how law-relative regret changes capacity and positioning choices relative to sample-average and worst-cost planning. We apply the decision tree to several years of New York fleet data, including the year before Hurricane Sandy, and to two emergency-service events. The test flags the pre-Sandy year as exposed. The training-support regret bounds cover realized test regret in three of four fleet folds. On Ida, where the regret-robust allocation differed from the sample-average one, it moved units toward the boroughs the storm loaded and cost less than the sample-average design.

papers.title: Automorphisms and Hodge isometries of surfaces with $K^2=p_g=1$
papers.authors: Jorge Duque Franco, Alvaro Liendo, Pedro Montero
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a minimal complex surface of general type with $K_S^2=p_g(S)=1$. By a theorem of Catanese, the canonical model of $S$ is a complete intersection of two sextics in $\mathbf{P}(1,2,2,3,3)$ whose equations admit a normal form, and the global Torelli theorem fails for these surfaces. We describe $\operatorname{Aut}(S)$ in terms of the coefficients of the normal form, prove that $|\operatorname{Aut}(S)|\leq 72$, and classify the surfaces attaining the bound: two surfaces with singular canonical model and a one-parameter family $X_r$ of smooth surfaces. For the surfaces $X_r$ we compute a basis of the primitive cohomology consisting of eigenvectors of a subgroup $\mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z} \times \mathbf{Z}/6\mathbf{Z}$ of $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$, given by residues of explicit polynomials, together with the intersection form in this basis. We then show that the natural map from $\operatorname{Aut}(X_r)$ to the group of Hodge isometries of the primitive lattice modulo $\pm1$ is injective but has image of index at least $331\,776$, so that the Torelli principle for automorphisms fails for these surfaces.

papers.title: Pinching Antenna and Relay Assisted Joint Indoor Outdoor NOMA Communications with SWIPT
papers.authors: Amit Agarwal, Susmita Sain, Keshav Singh, Sudip Biswas
papers.abstract: This paper investigates physical layer security in waveguide-based pinching antenna systems with a mobile eavesdropper. Assuming perfect knowledge of the legitimate user's location and only statistical information about the eavesdropper's position, the ergodic secrecy rate is analyzed under Gaussian and practical finite-alphabet signaling. Since the exact ergodic secrecy rate does not admit a tractable closed-form expression, a closed-form analytical upper bound is derived using Jensen's inequality. The resulting expression serves as an efficient objective for antenna position optimization without requiring exhaustive Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results verify the tightness of the proposed upper bound and show that the optimized antenna position closely matches the optimum obtained from Monte Carlo optimization. Furthermore, practical finite-alphabet signaling is shown to exhibit secrecy-rate saturation at high SNR, identifying an effective operating SNR region. Although the antenna position is optimized using the Gaussian-based upper bound, it remains effective for practical signaling.

papers.title: Initial Data Gluing for Asymptotically Hyperbolic Spacetimes
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of Corvino-Schoen-type gluing, also known as gluing up to linear obstructions, for asymptotically hyperbolic spacetimes satisfying appropriate smallness conditions in arbitrary dimension. The results retrieve and improve on previous known smallness requirements on initial data to conduct such gluing, including the work of Chrusci\'el and Delay. Our technique is highly versatile and well-suited for gluing results in highly anisotropic geometric settings.

papers.title: Classical cumulants from the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra
papers.abstract: We realize classical cumulants and their fixed-point equations in the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra introduced by Ebrahimi-Fard and Patras, placing classical, free, Boolean, and monotone cumulants in a common algebraic framework. A concatenation perturbation of the functionals yields left and right half-shuffle equations on ordinary words without changing the coproduct or either half-coproduct. Both equations are equivalent to the classical moment--cumulant formula and uniquely determine the classical cumulants. We also obtain a Hopf-algebraic realization of the classical-to-free cumulant transform through convolution exponentiation and the left half-shuffle logarithm. A commutative diagram identifies its partition-level action with summation over non-crossing closure fibers, recovering Lehner's closure-fiber formula within the framework of the double tensor unshuffle Hopf algebra.

papers.title: Absolutely universal projective embeddings of long-root geometries of orthogonal type
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $\Gamma$ its long-root geometry, namely $\Gamma$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $\Gamma$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $\Gamma$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $\Gamma$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $\Gamma$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $\Gamma$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $\Gamma$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $\Gamma$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.

papers.title: Robust augmented Block Preconditioning for two-phase Incompressible Inductionless MHD
papers.authors: Bijie Song, Lingxiao Li, Jie Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a robust augmented block preconditioner for three-dimensional, two-phase, incompressible inductionless MHD equations. We employ a high-order monolithic and charge-conservative arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) finite element method as base scheme, for which the solution variables are current density, velocity, electric potential and pressure. Grad-div stabilization is added in both the current density equation and discrete momentum equation. Backward Euler method is used for the time discretization. At each time step, fully coupled solution strategy is adopted. This leads to large-scale, ill-conditioned, nonsymmetric, and indefinite dual saddle-point system. To solve this system efficiently, we construct an augmented block preconditioner within the constraint preconditioning framework. The ultimate preconditioner combines the augmented Lagrangian technique with approximate block factorization for current density sub-system and fluid sub-system. The fully coupled four-field system is then solved using preconditioned FGMRES iteration. Numerical experiments confirm the high-order accuracy and discrete charge conservation of the ALE-FEM. Drop of heavy fluid in light fluid is taken as benchmark to demonstrate the robustness of the preconditioner with respect to the discontinuity of physical parameters and the mesh size.

papers.title: Rigidity of Convex Entire Solutions to Sum Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We study the rigidity of convex entire solutions to sum Hessian equations. Using a dimension-lifting identity, we reduce the problem to a standard \(k\)-Hessian equation in one higher dimension. By applying existing rigidity theorems, we prove that every \(C^2\) convex entire solution is a quadratic polynomial for \(2\leq k\leq n\), \(\alpha\geq0\), and a positive constant right-hand side, without any growth assumption at infinity. We also discuss the linear case \(k=1\).

papers.title: Observability Inequalities for Degenerate Schr\"odinger Equations via a Shape Approximation Method
papers.authors: Dong-Hui Yang, Hongli Sun, Weijia Wu, Yuanzhi Zhou
papers.abstract:
We study a two-dimensional Schr\"odinger equation with a boundary degeneracy. More precisely, the diffusion matrix is given by $
  A=\operatorname{diag}(1,x_2^\alpha), \alpha\in(0,1)$,
  so that the partial differential operator degenerates on a portion of the boundary. The main objective is to establish a boundary observability inequality for the corresponding degenerate Schr\"odinger equation.
  To overcome the difficulties caused by the boundary degeneracy, we introduce a shape design and approximation procedure. By removing a thin neighborhood of the degenerate boundary, we construct a family of uniformly Schr\"odinger equations on perturbed domains. We first investigate the spectral properties of the associated operators and establish the convergence of the approximate problems to the original degenerate problem. We then derive a boundary observability inequality for the uniformly approximating equations and pass to the limit as the thickness of the removed boundary layer tends to zero. This yields a boundary observability inequality for the original degenerate Schr\"odinger equation.
  Our approach combines spectral analysis, separation of variables, and shape design techniques. By employing multiplier methods for the uniformly approximating problems and passing to the degenerate limit, we establish the boundary observability inequality for the original degenerate Schr\"odinger equation.

papers.title: A quasi-polynomial $\chi$-bound for $P_6$-free graphs
papers.authors: Shenwei Huang, Yidong Zhou, Yuwen Zhou
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that every graph $G$ with no induced six-vertex path satisfies $\chi(G)\le \omega(G)^{c\log_2\omega(G)}$ for $c=45/\log_2(4/3)<109$. The best previous bound was exponential in $\omega(G)$. Our result is the first quasi-polynomial bound for $P_6$-free graphs and generalizes the bound for $P_5$-free graphs by Scott, Seymour, and Spirkl [Polynomial bounds for chromatic number. {IV}. {A} near-polynomial bound for excluding the five-vertex path. {\em Combinatorica}, 43(5):845--852, 2023].

papers.title: Volume of area-bounded PGL3-Hitchin moduli space
papers.authors: Qiongling Li, Beibei Liu, Weixu Su, Zhe Sun
papers.abstract: For the $\mathrm{PGL}_3$-Hitchin moduli space of unmarked convex $\mathbb{RP}^2$ structures on the surface $S_{g,m}$ with fixed boundary data $\mathbf L$ when $m>0$, we investigate the subset whose canonical Hilbert--Busemann area is bounded above by $t$. We show that the Goldman symplectic volume of this subset is at most $C_{g,m}(t+\lambda^2)^{8g-8+3m}$, where $\lambda$ is the largest total-root boundary length for $m>0$ and is set to $0$ for $m=0$. As a consequence, We obtain the explicit upper bound for the $e^{-s\cdot\mathrm{Area}}$-weighted volume.

papers.title: An exact compression-and-lifting procedure and D-optimal designs of orders 198 and 170
papers.abstract: We develop a compression-and-lifting procedure for constructing D-optimal complementary pairs on finite abelian groups of odd order. The procedure separates the Fourier conditions preserved by compression from those needed to recover the original binary sequences. For groups with a cyclic factor of order nine, integer matching conditions separate compatible classes of local sign assignments.
