Their exact sizes can be computed before full sequences are generated, allowing searches to discard incompatible pairs and select manageable classes. A bound on cosets on which a sequence is constant also excludes certain automorphisms as fixing symmetries. Applying the method yields supplementary difference sets with parameters $(99;43,42;36)$ and $(85;39,34;31)$, resolving two previously undecided parameter sets. These give the first D-optimal matrix of order $198$ and constructions with new parameters at the known order $170$. For the successful length-$99$ compression, the exact class condition removes $99.9888\%$ of candidate pairs while preserving every D-optimal lift. A reflection-invariant construction at length $85$ gives seven supplementary difference set classes and fourteen matrix classes under signed row and column permutations, paired by transposition. The class reductions guide computation; finding suitable compressions and matching their lifts remain search problems.

papers.title: Orthograph related to mutual (strong) numerical radius orthogonality on operator algebra
papers.authors: Shaoxing Sun, Jinchuan Hou, Xiaofei Qi
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{B} (H)$ and $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on a complex Hilbert space $H$ and the Jordan algebra of all self-adjoint operators in $\mathcal{B} (H)$, respectively. In this paper, the orthographs by (strong) numerical radius orthogonality relation on $\mathcal{B} (H)$ or $\mathcal{B} _s(H)$ is introduced, and then the graph-theoretic properties of these orthographs, such as isolated vertices, connected components and the diameters, are discussed.

papers.title: Noncommutative algebraic sets are not generically nc manifolds
papers.abstract: A consequence of implicit function theorem is that any algebraic set is a complex manifold except at some singular points which form a strictly lower dimension algebraic subset. Accordingly, an non commutative implicit function theorem of Agler-McCarthy might suggest that a nc algebraic set is generically an nc manifold. However, in this paper, a type of nc polynomials is shown, whose zero locus has larger dimension than the nc manifold given by implicit function theorem.

papers.title: An upper bound on the smallest singular value of dense signed random combinatorial matrices
papers.authors: Yuxiao Shi, Zeyan Song, Kexin Yu, Tingzhou Yu
papers.abstract: Let $M_n$ be an $n\times n$ random matrix with entries in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$, where each row is independently and uniformly sampled from the set of all vectors in $\{-1, 0, 1\}^n$ containing exactly $d$ nonzero entries, with $d=pn$ for some fixed constant $p\in(0,1/2]$. A recent result by one of the authors gives a lower bound of order $n^{-1/2}$ for the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of this model with high probability. In this paper, we establish a matching upper bound for $s_n(M_n)$. Specifically, there exists a constant $C_p>0$ depending only on $p$ such that \[ \forall \varepsilon >0 \qquad \mathbb{P} \left( s_n(M_n) \le \frac{\sqrt{d}}{\varepsilon^2 n} \right) \ge 1-C_p\left(\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\right). \] Consequently, in the dense regime, the smallest singular value $s_n(M_n)$ of signed random combinatorial matrices is typically of order $n^{-1/2}$.

papers.title: Quantum harmonic analysis and the Differential operators on weighted Bergman spaces of bounded symmetric domains
papers.authors: Matthew Dawson, Vishwa Dewage, Gestur Olafsson
papers.abstract:
We develop quantum harmonic analysis (QHA) for operators on the parametrized Bergman space $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$ of a bounded symmetric domain $\Omega$, extending the theory previously known for the unit ball. Building on this framework, we introduce a class of differential operators acting on operators on $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$. Combining these tools, we advance the theory of Toeplitz operators on $\mathcal{A}^2_
u(\Omega)$: we establish Toeplitz approximation results via the $\alpha$-Berezin transform, construct a differential operator $D_\alpha$ that shifts the $\alpha$-Berezin transform, and obtain several characterizations of the radial Toeplitz algebra -- including one via the uniformly continuous radial operators, and one via the domain of $D_\alpha$.

papers.title: Extremals for Trudinger-Moser inequalities via polygonal profiles
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish the existence of extremal functions for the Trudinger--Moser inequality with logarithmic weights $(-\log |x|)^{\beta}$ in two dimensions throughout the full range $0\le \beta<1$. We also extend recent results on the existence of local maximizers for the Trudinger--Moser functional beyond the critical threshold. Our approach uses polygonal profiles to establish a lower bound uniform in the weight parameter. An explicit thirty-node profile gives the lower bound $\mathrm{TM}_{4\pi}>4.38421793217\,\pi$ for the classical critical supremum on the unit disk, improving on the value $4.3556\,\pi$ obtained in the computer experiments of Carleson and Chang. This lower bound has a purely analytic proof, which uses only elementary inequalities and exact rational arithmetic. Numerical experiments with polygonal profiles of up to $102400$ nodes suggest that this lower bound can be raised to $4.402732044\,\pi$, which improves the recent computational lower bound by Li and Sun.

papers.title: Optimization-based Cell Average Limiters as Metric Projections: Constrained Evolution and Convergence Analysis for Convection-diffusion Equations
papers.authors: Seungmin Lee, Sanghyun Lee, Chen Liu
papers.abstract: The optimization-based cell average limiter enforces global conservation and bounds, and has been successfully applied to discontinuous Galerkin (DG) discretizations of a wide range of nonlinear systems, from phase-field models to the compressible Navier-Stokes equations. In this paper, taking the heat and convection-diffusion equations as prototypes, we analyze the convergence of the scheme resulting from cell average limiting. Encoding conservation and admissibility in a differential inclusion identifies the limiter as a backward Euler proximal step in a Lie splitting of the constrained evolution. This proximal step is the metric projection onto the convex admissible set, and we prove that it is nonexpansive and stable in the $L^2$ norm, and that it does not increase the total variation of the cell averages. Combined with the standard error analysis, nonexpansiveness yields an $O(\tau+h^{k+1})$ estimate for implicit Euler time stepping with DG discretization of polynomial degree $k$ under a reverse CFL condition, together with an unconditional $O(\tau+h^{k})$ estimate. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted convergence rates and the enforcement of the bounds.

papers.title: Coordinate systems and maximal order complexity in Banach lattices
papers.authors: A. Avil\'es, C. Rosendal, M. A. Taylor, P. Tradacete
papers.abstract: We resolve three questions arising from the study of coordinate systems and order convergence in Banach lattices. Firstly, every order (respectively, $\sigma$-order) basis $(e_n)$ for a Banach lattice $X=[e_n]$ is automatically a Schauder basis. In fact, the associated partial sum projections satisfy a maximal inequality, and hence every such basis is uniform. Secondly, we show that there is a separable Banach lattice $X$ in which the set $$ X_{\downarrow0}=\{(x_n)\in X^{\mathbb N}:x_1\geqslant x_2\geqslant\ldots\geqslant 0=\inf_nx_n\} $$ is $\mathbf{\Pi}^1_1$-complete. Finally, we construct a separable Banach lattice $Y$ for which the set $Y^{\uparrow\infty}$ of increasing positive sequences which are not order bounded is $\mathbf{\Pi}^1_1$-complete. It follows that neither $X_{\downarrow0}$ nor $Y^{\uparrow\infty}$ can be described in any simpler way than by the nonexistence of positive lower and upper bounds, respectively.

papers.title: Delambre--Gauss Formulas in Complex Hyperbolic Space
papers.abstract: We establish a Delambre--Gauss matrix identity for oriented right-angled hexagons in the complex hyperbolic plane. The six complex length parameters of a hexagon determine two alternating \(3\times3\) matrices whose product is central in (\mathrm{SU}(2,1)\). The resulting nine entry-wise equations extend the Delambre-Gauss formula of Tan, Wong, and Zhang in 4-dimensional hyperbolic geometry to this complex hyperbolic setting.

papers.title: Hitchin's $\alpha$-invariant and positive sectional curvature on homotopy $9$-spheres
papers.authors: Yang-Hui He, Ziran Liu, Shing-Tung Yau
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth homotopy $9$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of positive sectional curvature if and only if its Hitchin $\alpha$-invariant vanishes, or equivalently if and only if it admits a Riemannian metric of positive scalar curvature.

papers.title: A Twisted Affine Interpolation of the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded Integrable Super-Liouville and super-Sinh-Gordon Equations
papers.authors: Naruhiko Aizawa, Ren Ito, Luiza Miranda, Francesco Toppan
papers.abstract: This paper is a third one in a series devoted to the construction of $2D$, $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded, integrable Toda field theories. The first paper introduced parabosonic models obtained from Rittenberg-Wyler color Lie algebras; the second paper explained how to deal with parafermions (the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded super-Liouville theory) from finite Rittenberg-Wyler color Lie superalgebras. This new paper extends the construction to the infinite case of (twisted) affine color Lie superalgebras. A $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded extension of ${\widehat{\mathfrak{osp}(2|2)^{(2)}}}$ allows to interpolate the super-Liouville and the super-Sinh-Gordon models, recovered as special limits. The $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded extensions of three frameworks are here discussed: the Polyakov's soldering, the Leznov-Savel'ev Lax pair (zero-curvature) formulation and the B\"acklund transformations. As a byproduct of the construction, the Hamiltonian reduction from the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded ${\widehat{\mathfrak{osp(2|2)}^{(2)}}}$ WZNW models induces a $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded color Lie superalgebra which admits three inequivalent superVirasoro subalgebras; they are the ${\cal N}=2$ superVirasoro, the $(1,\frac{3}{2},\frac{3}{2},2)$ $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded superVirasoro and the $(\frac{3}{2},\frac{3}{2},2,2)$ $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded superVirasoro.

papers.title: Parabolic filtrations of Soergel bimodules
papers.abstract: Given a Coxeter system $(W,S)$ and a subset $I\subset S$. Let $W_I=\langle I\rangle$ be the standard parabolic subgroup of a Coxeter group $W$, and ${}^IW$ be the set of representatives of minimal length in the coset $W_I\backslash W$. We construct a parabolic version of Soergel's standard filtration, and show that, given any Soergel bimodule, each subquotient of its parabolic filtration is a direct sum of grading shifts of $B_x^I\otimes_R R_y$ with $x\in W_I$ and $y\in {}^IW$. By applying the character theorem of Elias and Williamson, we deduce the positivity of coefficients in the expansion of $C_w$ with respect to the hybrid basis $\{C_xT_y:x\in W_I,y\in {}^IW\}$. This generalizes Grojnowski and Haiman's result to any Coxeter group.

papers.title: Proof of the Langberg-M\'edard Multiple Unicast Conjecture
papers.authors: Kai Cai, Guangyue Han, Mengxi Yang, Wenan Zang
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}=(V,A,S, R)$ be a directed network, where $D=(V,A)$ is a digraph, $S=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of senders, and $R=\{r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of receivers. We prove that if, for each $1\le j \le k$, there exist $k$ pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in $D$, one from each $s_i$ to $r_j$, then the underlying undirected network of ${\cal N}$, with unit capacities, admits a feasible $(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k)$-$(r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k)$ multiflow of value $1$ for each pair $(s_i,r_i)$, $i=1,2,\ldots,k$. This establishes the multiple unicast conjecture proposed by Langberg and M\'edard in 2009.

papers.title: A secondary term in the first moment of cubic $L$-functions over function fields
papers.abstract: Let $q$ be a fixed odd prime power with $q\equiv2\pmod3$. We study the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\Fq(T)$, ordered by their genus. By averaging the rational sieve variable in the double Dirichlet series of Hong and Fang, we obtain meromorphic continuation beyond the secondary polar divisor. Combining this continuation with the cubic Gauss-sum residues computed by David, Florea and Lal\'in gives an explicit term of order $q^{5g/6}$, with a real coefficient depending on $g$ modulo $6$, and an error $O_{q,\eps}(q^{(23/28+\eps)g})$. The periodic coefficient is not identically zero. The proof uses an exact first difference supplied by the functional equation, an Euler product for the sieve average, and Bochner's tube theorem in the Dirichlet variables.

papers.title: On some bounds for cardinal invariants of the space of quasicontinuous functions with the topology of pointwise convergence
papers.abstract: In this paper, we obtain some bounds for cardinal invariants such as character, pseudocharacter, tightness, {L}indel\"of number, hereditary {L}indel\"of number, hereditary density and spread of $Q_p(X,Y)$, the space of all quasicontinuous functions from $X$ to $Y$ equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence. We prove that the tightness, hereditary {L}indel\"of number, hereditary density and spread of the space $Q_p(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ are equal to the cardinality of $\mathbb{R}$.

papers.title: Blow-up analysis and compactness for critical Dirac equations on $\mathbb S^n$
papers.abstract:
We study blow-up and compactness for the critical nonlinear Dirac equation \[ D_{g_0}\psi_i =
H_i|\psi_i|^{\frac{2}{n-1}}\psi_i \qquad \text{on }\mathbb S^n,\quad n\ge 3, \] where $g_0$ is the round metric and $H_i\to H>0$ in $C^0(\mathbb S^n)$. Under a first-threshold bound on the critical mass, we prove that every blowing-up sequence has, after passing to a subsequence, a unique blow-up point $p$ satisfying $H(p)=\max_{\mathbb S^n}H$. The rescaled solutions converge to a ground-state Dirac bubble that carries the entire limiting critical mass. Under local uniform $C^1$ bounds on $H_i$, we use the Kelvin transform and a second rescaling to prove that $p$ is an isolated simple blow-up point. We also derive sharp pointwise and gradient estimates in cylindrical coordinates and identify the normalized Green limit.
  If the coefficients converge in $C^2$ near $p$, the Pohozaev identity yields $\operatorname{Hess}_{g_0}H(p)=0$. Consequently, if a positive $H\in C^2(\mathbb S^n)$ satisfies $\Delta_{g_0}H(p)<0$ at every global maximum, then solutions with critical mass bounded by a level slightly above the first threshold are uniformly bounded in $L^\infty(\mathbb S^n)$. This bound remains uniform under small $C^2$ perturbations of $H$.

papers.title: Ambient Chain-Relation Reduction in Contracting Controlled Skew-Product Semiflows
papers.abstract: The qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations is often studied through cocycles and skew-product semiflows over a driving base. We develop a chain-recurrence reduction principle for systems admitting an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking. The abstract theorem determines the complete chain-attainability relation in the ambient phase space: chains may start off the attracting section, but every attainable target lies on it and is selected solely by the factor semiflow. Applied to contracting controlled skew-product semiflows, this gives exact descriptions of the chain recurrent set, chain components, Conley order, compact strictly invariant sets, attractors, basins, and dual repellers. A weighted-supremum transverse gauge yields a complete Lyapunov function for the full semiflow while preserving the recurrent values of the base. The differential hypotheses are verified through subadditive fiber-derivative growth and averaged moving-metric logarithmic norms, allowing transient expansion and non-unique ergodicity. Quantitative persistence is established for finite-window maps and smooth vector-field perturbations. The results provide a unified framework for chain recurrence, Lyapunov structure, and attractor--repeller geometry in contracting nonautonomous dynamics.

papers.title: Path space large deviation on a lattice for interacting particle systems
papers.abstract:
We investigate the path space large deviation principle (LDP) for a class of interacting particle systems on a fixed finite discrete torus. As an illustrative example, we use the partial exclusion process with maximal occupation of $s$ particles. We first verify the standard Kurtz-type law of large numbers for the original and tilted processes, thereby identifying the deterministic flows around which the large deviations are formulated. We then establish the path space LDP, with speed $s$, and identify the associated rate function in variational form as the Legendre transform of a nonlinear Hamiltonian. The proof relies on martingale techniques, exponential tightness, and a change-of-measure argument based on exponential tilting, which renders atypical trajectories typical under a modified dynamics.
  We also explain how the same strategy extends to further interacting particle systems. The inclusion process illustrates the conservative non-compact finite-jump case. The harmonic process is qualitatively different: a single transition may move a variable number of particles, and the limiting Hamiltonian is logarithmic with a non-trivial domain. This places the harmonic process outside the usual finite-reaction framework for density-dependent Markov jump processes. Finally, we discuss continuous-state energy-exchange models, such as the Brownian energy process and an integrable heat-conduction model, to indicate how the same Hamiltonian large-deviation formalism appears beyond discrete-state particle systems.

papers.title: Mass concentration and ground states of Fermi systems in Hartree--Fock model with potentials
papers.authors: Zhuocheng Li, Yuan-da Wu, Xiaoyu Zeng
papers.abstract: Understanding the onset and mechanism of collapse at critical attractive interaction is a fundamental problem in the variational theory of finite fermionic systems. In this paper, we study this problem within the Hartree--Fock framework under various trapping potentials. By establishing a finite-rank Hartree-type Gagliardo--Nirenberg--Sobolev inequality, we identify a critical threshold $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$ governing the existence of ground states. We then determine the concentration behavior of ground states as the interaction parameter approaches $\mathcal{K}^{(N)}$. To reveal how the geometry of the trap influences this critical phenomenon, we consider three representative classes of potentials: polynomial-type potentials, ring-shaped potentials, and potentials whose zero set has nonempty interior. For each class, we derive the concentration scale and sharp asymptotics of the least energy. The resulting regimes are qualitatively different, showing that both the location and the rate of concentration are selected by the local geometry of the potential near its minimum set. In contrast to scalar Hartree problems, the nonlocal interaction is coupled here with pairwise $L^2$-orthogonality constraints, and their interplay creates substantial difficulties in the compactness and blow-up analysis.

papers.title: Some chromatic height computations for homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology
papers.abstract: For an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum $R$ of chromatic height $k$, the trace method and the chromatic redshift imply that $T^n$-fixed point of $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology of $R$ has chromatic height at most $k+n$. In this paper, we compute these heights for $H\mathbb{F}_p$, $H\mathbb{Z}$ and the $p$-complete connective image-of-$J$ spectrum $j_p$ for all primes and $n\geq1$, which are exactly $n-1$, $n$ and $n+1$, respectively. Our method is based on properties of Wilson spaces and relative topological Hochschild homology over $\mathrm{MU}$.

papers.title: An improved fast iterative moment method for the simulation of near-continuum gas flows with Shakhov model
papers.authors: Zhenning Cai, Zhicheng Hu, Guanghan Li, Chunwu Wang, Xiaowen Wang
papers.abstract: The fast iterative moment (FIM) method developed in [G. Li, C. Wang, and Z. Hu, Comput. Fluids, 311 (2026), 107031] achieves fast convergence for near-continuum gas flows modeled by the Boltzmann-BGK equation through alternating iterations between the high-order moment system and the consistent hydrodynamic equations. In this paper, we extend the FIM solver to the Shakhov model and improve it in the following aspects. A finite volume method with linear reconstruction is employed for high-resolution spatial discretization of both systems. Following the original FIM method, an implicit-explicit scheme treating the Shakhov collision term implicitly is adopted for the high-order moment system. A local Fourier analysis of a linearized one-dimensional BGK model reveals the need for more hydrodynamic iterations at smaller Knudsen numbers and their slower convergence on refined grids. Motivated by these findings, a Newton-multigrid method with a new regularization strategy is introduced for the hydrodynamic equations, generally providing an effective hydrodynamic correction with one step per alternating iteration, thereby reducing the need for empirical tuning. Numerical experiments for planar Couette flow, lid-driven cavity flow, and heat transfer in a bottom-heated cavity are carried out to investigate the performance of the improved FIM solver. The results demonstrate improved efficiency and robustness over the original FIM method, particularly at small Knudsen numbers, and favorable performance with both first- and second-order spatial discretizations.

papers.title: On the enriched approximate completeness
papers.abstract:
We generalize to the enriched setting the classical theorem of Freyd, that the free cocompletion ${\mathscr PA}$ of a category ${\mathscr A}$ is complete if and only if ${\mathscr A}$ is approximately complete.
  The work of Day and Lack, arXiv:math/0610439, has laid the foundations for such a generalization and has had multiple applications in homotopy theory and in category theory. Our result allows us to expand on some of these applications.

papers.title: Uniform boundary observability for periodic waves, I: up to the $\varepsilon^{-1}$ eigenvalue scale
papers.authors: Jun Geng, Shumao Wang, Wei Wang
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon=-\operatorname{div}(A(x/\varepsilon)\nabla)$ be a scalar divergence-form operator on a bounded $C^3$ domain, where $A$ is symmetric, uniformly elliptic, Lipschitz continuous, and periodic. For initial data spectrally truncated at the eigenvalue level $N$, we establish whole-boundary observability and projected exact controllability, uniformly in the range $N\leq\delta\varepsilon^{-1}$. This extends the cutoff $N\lesssim\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ obtained by Lin and Shen (J. Eur. Math. Soc. 2022). The key input is a two-sided boundary estimate for fixed-width spectral packets of $\sqrt{\mathcal{L}_\varepsilon}$ at frequencies that satisfy $\varepsilon\mu^2\ll1$. Its lower bound combines quantitative Dirichlet corrector estimates with a forcing-stable microscopic boundary Cauchy estimate. Miller's spectral packet criterion and the Hilbert uniqueness method then convert this packet estimate into the corresponding wave results, with constants independent of $\varepsilon$ and $N$.

papers.title: Admissible Subspaces for the Collective Haar Twirl: Schur-Weyl Classification and Heredity under Tensor-Factor Reduction
papers.abstract: Quantum private broadcasting (\textsf{QPB}) asks whether a quantum message can be encrypted once, broadcast to several recipients, and decrypted locally while the joint ciphertext reveals no plaintext information. Broadbent, Gonz\'alez-Guill\'en, and Schuknecht showed that the full tensor-power space \(\mathcal H_d^{\otimes t}\) is generally unsuitable for \textsf{QPB}, identified \(\mathrm{Sym}^t(\mathcal H_d)\) as a natural plaintext space, introduced symmetric unitary \(t\)-designs, and asked which other subspaces support private broadcast. Using Schur-Weyl duality, we classify all subspaces \(\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal H_d^{\otimes t}\) on which the collective Haar twirl \(\mathcal T^{(t)}\) is a replacement channel. Precisely, every Schur-Weyl block weight must be independent of the encoded state, and in each active block \(V_\lambda\otimes W_\lambda\), the reduced state on the multiplicity space \(W_\lambda\) must be fixed. This yields explicit two-block and general multiblock constructions and realizes the classification as the Schur-Weyl form of the Knill-Laflamme conditions for a complementary channel of \(\mathcal T^{(t)}\). We also introduce a canonical reduction under deletion of a recipient and characterize privacy heredity, design heredity, and \textsf{QPB}-heredity for exact restricted designs. The symmetric tower is fully \textsf{QPB}-hereditary, whereas the antisymmetric tower is fully privacy-hereditary and is design-hereditary from level \(s\) to \(s-1\) exactly when \(s\leq(d+1)/2\). For canonical carriers in arbitrary Schur-Weyl blocks, hereditary reduction is governed by multiplicity-free branching along the Young graph and inclusion of the associated Peter-Weyl coefficient spaces.

papers.title: Joint End-to-End Training of Weighted BP Decoder Ensembles
papers.authors: Felix Krieg, Paul Bezner, Stephan ten Brink
papers.abstract: Ensemble decoding improves decoding reliability by combining component decoders with complementary failure events. Existing approaches typically obtain this diversity from code-specific structure, such as code automorphisms, multiple parity-check representations, or targeted modifications of the message-passing graph. In this work, we instead learn the diversity of an ensemble of weighted belief propagation decoders by jointly optimizing trainable Tanner-graph edge weights. A central design question is how the training objective should distribute gradient among the ensemble members to promote complementary decoding behavior. To this end, we compare four ensemble objectives under direct gradient-based optimization and identify best-member training as the most effective approach. For a (64,32) progressive edge-growth (PEG) low-density parity-check (LDPC) code, the resulting ensemble outperforms the considered trained and untrained belief-propagation-based ensemble baselines. With 10 members, it provides a gain of approximately 0.66 dB over a single belief propagation decoder at a target frame error rate (FER) of $10^{-4}$. Similar behavior is observed for a (128,64) CCSDS LDPC code, indicating that the learned complementarity is not specific to PEG. Although the ensemble performance improves substantially, all trained members show a higher standalone FER. The gain therefore results from learned specialization and complementary failure events rather than uniformly improved component decoders.

papers.title: Local obstructions and certified computations for perfect powers in power sums
papers.abstract: Let $S_k(x)=1^k+\cdots+x^k$. We study perfect-power values of $S_k(x)$ by combining local valuations with finite congruence certificates. For an irregular Bernoulli pair $(p,r)$ with $e=v_p(B_r)\ge1$, we prove a valuation formula uniform for $k\equiv r+1\pmod{p^e(p-1)}$, subject to an explicit condition on $v_p(x(x+1))$. This gives explicit families of nonexistence results in which both $x$ and $k$ are unbounded. We also determine all solutions of $S_k(x)=y^n$ for $3\le x\le10^6$ with $x\equiv0,3\pmod4$, leaving $k$ and $n\ge2$ unrestricted and including squares. This extends Hajdu's fixed-$x$ classification in the same residue classes. A uniform restriction on the normalized odd part of $S_k(x)$ and finite certificates exclude every $k\ge6$; the remaining exponents are checked by exact integer arithmetic. The certificates admit independent verification. We further prove a limitation of congruence tests of bounded prime-power depth and solve the equation for every $x\equiv28\pmod{5\,110\,664}$.

papers.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $\lambda_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}\lambda_1(f)^n$ if $\lambda_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $\lambda_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.

papers.title: Concave entire solutions of the Liouville equation
papers.authors: Changfeng Gui, Qinfeng Li, Chunhua Wang, Lu Xu
papers.abstract: We prove that every concave entire solution of the Liouville equation $-\Delta u=e^{2u}$ in $\R^n$ is one-dimensional, and we extend the result to a class of general semilinear equations under suitable conditions on the nonlinearity. In dimension two, we also provide a PDE-based proof of the known classification of quasiconcave solutions to planar Liouville solutions, without relying on complex-analytic methods developed in the previous work by Bergweiler-Eremenko-Langley \cite{BEL}

papers.title: Remarks on covariant differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s sphere
papers.abstract: An $SU_q(2)$-covariant first-order differential calculus on the non-standard quantum Podle\'s two-sphere is constructed. The module of one-forms is explicitly given in terms of modules of sections of charge $\pm 2$ line bundles associated to the quantum Hopf fibration.

papers.title: A note on Rota-Baxter affgebras
papers.abstract: An affinization of a concept of a Rota-Baxter operator or Rota-Baxter affgebras are discussed. Rota-Baxter Lie affgebras and their relation to Rota-Baxter Lie algebras are treated in more detail. In particular it is shown that every Rota-Baxter Lie affgebra is isomorphic to a Rota-Baxter Lie affgebra with a Lie algebra fibre over which the affine Rota-Baxter operator is linear.

papers.title: Multiplicity of weak solutions for mixed variable exponent triharmonic problems with hardy potentials
papers.authors: Khalid Soualhine, Adnane Belakhdar, Mohamed karim Hamdani
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of a nonlinear boundary value problem driven by a combination of mixed variable-exponent triharmonic operators and a Hardy-type singular potential. Specifically, we consider \[ \begin{cases} -a(x)\,\Delta_{p(x)}^{3}u - b(x)\,\Delta_{q(x)}^{3}u + m(x)\,\dfrac{|u|^{s(x)-2}u}{|x|^{3s(x)}} = \mu f(x,u), & \text{in } \Omega, \\ u = \Delta u = \Delta^{2}u = 0, & \text{on } \partial\Omega, \end{cases} \] where $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a smooth bounded domain with $N > 3$. The operators $\Delta_{p(x)}^{3}$ and $\Delta_{q(x)}^{3}$ represent triharmonic operators with variable exponents, creating a framework of nonstandard growth. Under suitable assumptions on the variable exponents $p(x), q(x), s(x)$, the weight functions $a(x), b(x), m(x)$, and the nonlinearity $f(x,u)$, we establish the existence of at least three distinct weak solutions. Our approach is variational, relying on critical point theory for functionals defined on variable-exponent Sobolev spaces. By combining Ricceri's and Bonanno-Marano's abstract three critical points theorems with new Hardy-Rellich inequalities adapted to the variable-exponent setting, we prove our main multiplicity result for small values of the parameter $\mu$. To our knowledge, this work presents the first systematic treatment of sixth-order problems featuring simultaneously mixed variable exponents and Hardy-type singular potentials.

papers.title: Boundedness of the Density of Wiener Functionals with Low Regularity
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that if a Wiener functional $F$ is $1+\delta$-differentiable in the Malliavin sense for some $\delta>0$ and satisfies the nondegeneracy condition, then the density of the law of $F$ exists, is bounded and is H\"{o}lder continuous of every exponent $\beta<\delta$. This gives a partial positive answer to a problem proposed by Watanabe [13]; to date, this seems to be the best result available for the boundedness of the density of Wiener functionals. The approach is based on the fractional order Sobolev spaces associated with a probability measure and on the Riesz transform.

papers.title: Ordinary algebras of complex-valued functions
papers.abstract: A classical theorem due to Gleason, Kahane, and Zelazko states that every complex unital Banach algebra is ordinary, meaning that any linear functional mapping elements into their spectrum is a character. While Roitman and Sternfeld extended this property to algebras with bounded spectra-showing in particular that the algebra C(X) of continuous functions is ordinary when X is pseudocompact-the general case of C(X) for arbitrary topological spaces X appears to be open, as we could not locate any reference in this direction. In this paper, we show that the pseudocompactness condition is unnecessary, that is, C(X) is ordinary for every topological space X. This fact is obtained as a consequence of a more general result characterizing positive characters on a purely algebraic generalization of unital C*-algebras, which we introduce under the name of AC*-algebras. As applications, we obtain two necessary and sufficient conditions for a Tychonoff space X to be realcompact in terms of 1-evaluating linear functionals on C(X) and their continuity with respect to the compact-open topology. Finally, we establish a Banach--Stone type theorem showing that two realcompact spaces X and Y are homeomorphic if and only if C(X) and C(Y) are linearly isomorphic via a map that preserves invertibility.

papers.title: A structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems
papers.abstract: Recently, the author refuted several conjectures about the vanishing of multiple correlation sequences. The goal of this paper is to provide a counterpart for the conjectures of Frantzikinakis--Kuca and of Leibman. The significance of this manuscript is twofold: firstly, we provide a structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems along arithmetic progressions (in the sense of Frantzikinakis--Kuca), and a corresponding structure theorem for polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds in connected nilmanifolds (in the sense of Leibman). Secondly, we identify null generalized nilsequences, as a notion of smallness, which provides a structured counterpart for null sequences. In particular, in the special case of ergodic nilsystems, we answer positively a question of Frantzikinakis on the structure of multiple correlation sequences.

papers.title: Searching for binary orientable sequences
papers.abstract: An aperiodic binary orientable sequence is a finite sequence of zeros and ones for which, for some integer $n$, all the subsequences of $n$ consecutive symbols, read either forwards or backwards, are distinct. Analogously, a periodic binary orientable sequence is an infinite periodic sequence of zeros and ones for which, for some integer $n$, all the subsequences of $n$ consecutive symbols, read either forwards or backwards, are distinct within a single period of the sequence. Such sequences have potential application in position-location applications. For applications, the longer the sequence (or the greater the period in the periodic case) the greater its utility, but yet while constructions are known for such sequences, and upper bounds on their length (or period) exist, the precise maximum length (or period) was previously unknown for anything other than small values of $n$. In this note the results of LLM-conducted searches for the longest possible aperiodic and periodic binary orientable sequences for $n\leq16$ are reported. In each case an example of a sequence of the maximum discovered length is also provided, and the maximum possible length is now determined for every $n\leq16$ for both the periodic and aperiodic cases.

papers.title: GKZ Systems and Gauss-Manin Connections of Families of Projective Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: Periods of projective hypersurfaces satisfy GKZ hypergeometric systems, which may have solutions that do not arise as periods. For deformations of Fermat hypersurfaces, we describe the Gauss-Manin connection in terms of images of contiguity operators between GKZ systems. These images are also realized as Fourier transforms of minimal extensions of Kummer modules.

papers.title: Asymptotic expansions for random walks conditioned to stay positive with arbitrary endpoints
papers.abstract: We consider a one-dimensional random walk $S_n$ with i.i.d. integer-valued increments having zero mean and finite variance. Under suitable moment assumptions, we derive asymptotic expansions for the local probabilities $\pr(x+S_n=y,\tau_x>n)$, where $\tau_x=\inf\{n\ge1:x+S_n\le0\}$. These extend previous expansions for walks started at zero to arbitrary starting points. We obtain different expansions according to the sizes of the starting point and endpoint relative to $\sqrt n$.

papers.title: Counterexamples to congruences in finite p-groups
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a conjugacy class of a finite $p$-group $G$. H\'ethelyi, K\"ulshammer and the author asked whether the number of conjugacy classes contained in $KK^{-1}$ is always congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$, and whether, dually, the number of irreducible constituents of $\chi\overline{\chi}$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$ for every $\chi\in\mathrm{Irr}(G)$. We construct a group of order $7^7$ for which both congruences fail.

papers.title: Mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces
papers.abstract: Based on mixed-norm Herz spaces, we introduce a new class of mixed-norm Herz-type Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We establish their $\varphi$-transform characterization in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth and prove Sobolev embedding theorems for these spaces. The resulting embedding theorems extend and improve several known results for mixed-norm Triebel-Lizorkin spaces.

papers.title: Zeros of Melnikov functions for periodically perturbed Hamiltonian systems with random coefficients
papers.abstract: Introducing a probabilistic perspective on a classical theme within the study of chaotic dynamics, we investigate the zeros of the Melnikov distance function associated to a periodically perturbed Hamiltonian system when the perturbation has random coefficients. We provide asymptotic estimates (as the period of the perturbation becomes large or small) for the average number of zeros and for the probability of no zeros.

papers.title: Asymptotic analysis of Dirichlet problems in supercritically perforated domains via quantification by torsional rigidity
papers.abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem $-\mathrm{div}(A^{\varepsilon}\nabla u^{\varepsilon}) = f$ on varying open sets $D^{\varepsilon}$, with uniformly elliptic coefficients $A^{\varepsilon}$, in the regime where the solutions vanish in the limit for every source. For periodically perforated domains, this is the supercritical regime. We show that the torsional rigidity $T(D^{\varepsilon})$ is the natural normalization: up to a subsequence, $u^{\varepsilon}/T(D^{\varepsilon})$ converges weakly as measures to $kf$ for every continuous source $f$, where $k$ is a nonzero finite measure independent of $f$, which we call the effective measure. The key ingredient is an estimate comparing $u^{\varepsilon}$ with the product of $f$ and the torsion function, whose rate depends on the domains only through $T(D^{\varepsilon})$. We also show that this rate is optimal. No structural assumption on the perforation is needed, and the results hold for relaxed Dirichlet problems. Every nonzero finite measure arises as an effective measure, so the continuity of the source cannot be dropped in general. For rougher sources, we characterize the convergence by a condition on the domains alone, expressed through their torsion functions or, equivalently, their Poincar\'{e} constants. We also prove that the effective measure is local, satisfies optimal two-sided bounds and is monotone with respect to the coefficients, and we study the role of the antisymmetric parts of the coefficients.

papers.title: Squarefree Values of Random Polynomials
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider the error term in the expected count of squarefree values of a polynomial when evaluated at integers \(n\le N\). We prove a power saving on average over polynomials of fixed degree and height at most \(H\). Our results improve previous estimates of Browning and Shparlinski in that the required range of \(H\) is independent of the degree, but depends on \(N\)

papers.title: Prescribed spectral configurations under rank-one perturbations
papers.abstract:
A spectral configuration specifies the Fredholm set, the Fredholm index on each of its components, and, on zero-index components, either the whole component or a locally finite set of discrete eigenvalues with prescribed algebraic multiplicities. We show that any two spectral configurations with the same Fredholm set and index can be realized by a suitable closed operator \(A\) and a rank-one perturbation \(A+K\). This remains true even when the rank-one operator \(K\), acting on a given separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, is prescribed in advance. In particular, for any such prescribed \(K\), one can choose \(A\) such that the discrete eigenvalues of \(A+K\) accumulate at the common essential spectrum at any prescribed rate.
  The proof is inspired by classical linearization theory. The main tool is the fact that arbitrary holomorphic functions can be represented as rank-one perturbation determinants.

papers.title: On Lehmer's Problem
papers.abstract:
Let $m\geq 2$ be an integer, and let $d\geq 2$ be an even integer. We study monic, reciprocal, non-cyclotomic polynomials $$ P(x)=x^d+a_{d-1}x^{d-1}+\cdots+a_1x+1\in\mathbb{Z}[x]. $$ For a fixed residue class $r\in\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$, we prove that there exists an effectively computable constant $c_{r,m}>1$ such that the Mahler measure $$ M(P)\geq c_{r,m} $$ for every irreducible polynomial $Q$ whose inner coefficients satisfy $$ a_j\equiv r\pmod m \qquad (1\leq j\leq d-1). $$ Moreover, we explicitly compute the constant $c_{r,m}$ in terms of $r$ and $m$. For the residue classes $r=2$, $r=3$, and $r=m-1$, we obtain improved lower bounds for suitable ranges of the modulus~$m$.
  We also consider monic, reciprocal, irreducible, non-cyclotomic polynomials whose inner coefficients belong to two distinct residue classes modulo $m$. More precisely, if the inner coefficients with odd indices are congruent to $a\pmod m$ and those with even indices are congruent to $b\pmod m$, where $a\not\equiv b\pmod m$, then we prove the existence of a constant $c_{m,a,b}>1$ such that the Mahler measure $$ M(P)\geq c_{m,a,b}. $$ These results solve Lehmer's problem for several families of polynomials. We also construct infinitely many examples in every even degree $d\geq 2$ of monic, reciprocal, irreducible, non-cyclotomic polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}$, together with explicit information about their Mahler measures.
  Our proofs rely on Y. Bilu's equidistribution theorem and its effective version proved by C. D'Andrea \emph{et al.}, as well as on a method developed by P. Borwein \emph{et al.} While it is natural to consider Bilu's equidistribution results in conjunction with the Borwein {\it et al}. method to Lehmer's problem, we are not aware of any previous work in the literature that employs this particular approach.

papers.title: Approximate Controllability of Neutral Integro-Differential Inclusions Associated with Hemivariational Inequalities in Banach Spaces with Uniformly Convex Dual
papers.authors: Jyoti Jindal, Sumit Arora, Manil T. Mohan
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the approximate controllability of neutral integro-differential inclusions driven by hemivariational inequalities with nonlocal inclusion conditions in a Banach space $\mathbb{V}$ whose dual $\mathbb{V}^*$ is uniformly convex, using resolvent operator theory. We first establish an equivalence between the original problem and an associated differential inclusion involving the Clarke subdifferential. Under suitable assumptions, we then prove the existence of mild solutions corresponding to admissible controls in $\mathrm{L}^2(I,\mathbb{U})$. A key contribution of this work lies in the analysis of the control construction in Banach spaces, where the duality mapping $\mathcal{J} = \partial\big(\tfrac{1}{2}\|\cdot\|_{\mathbb{V}}^2\big)$ is generally nonlinear, in contrast to the Hilbert space setting, while such nonlinearity has been viewed as a technical obstruction in earlier studies. Based on this framework, we prove approximate controllability of the original system by relating it to the controllability of the associated linearized inclusion and constructing appropriate controls involving the duality mapping. Finally, we present applications to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: The closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a Z-set in the family of all bivariate Schur concave copulas, and related results
papers.abstract: Very recently, Problem 2.5 stated by Mesiar and Sarkoci in \cite{MeSa} and originally formulated by Durante was answered in the negative by \v{S}eliga \cite{Sel}. The author showed that the closed convex hull of all bivariate associative copulas is a proper subset of the family of all Schur concave copulas, and even computed the exact uniform distance of his counterexamples to the closed convex hull (so that the Hausdorff distance between the two families is at least $\frac32-\sqrt{2}$). Using the fact that every bivariate associative copula can be represented as a (finite or countably infinite) ordinal sum of Archimedean copulas and the minimum copula $M$, and working with the Markov kernels of Archimedean copulas, we first give an alternative, simple proof of the strict inclusion. We do so by showing that convex combinations of associative copulas can assign only very little mass to \new{staircase-shaped unions of small squares covering} certain line segments parallel to the main diagonal, a result we later extend to so-called chains and staircases. Building on the first observation, we then go one step further and show that, from a topological perspective, the closed convex hull of all associative copulas is a very small subset of the Schur concave family, namely a so-called $Z$-set, and that the family of associative copulas is, in turn, a $Z$-set in its closed convex hull.

papers.title: Zassenhaus Filtration and Ihara Constants
papers.authors: Liming Ma, Chaoping Xing, Zugan Xing
papers.abstract:
Let $X$ be a curve over $\mathbb{F}_q$. Denote by $N(X)$ and $g(X)$ the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and the genus of $X$ respectively. The Ihara constant \begin{equation*} A(q)=\limsup_{g(X)\to\infty}\frac{N(X)}{g(X)} \end{equation*} measures the asymptotic abundance of rational points on curves over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
  In this paper, we study the Zassenhaus filtration of pro-$p$ groups arising from class field towers. By combining Golod--Shafarevich theorem, embedding problems and central class field theory, we establish a new criterion for the infinitude of class field towers. As an application, we obtain an improvement on the best known lower bounds of Ihara constant $A(2)$ and $A(3)$ which are explicitly given by \[
  A(2)\geq 0.317779\cdots \text{ and }
  A(3)\geq 0.496074\cdots. \]

papers.title: Fractional reversible chemical kinetics: Time-Driven Monte Carlo method and application to enzyme conformational dynamics
papers.authors: Nelson H. T. Lemes, Higor V. M. Ferreira
papers.abstract: In this work, we present a fractional framework for reversible two-state chemical kinetics derived from the Continuous-Time Random Walk (CTRW) formalism with Mittag-Leffler waiting-time distributions. This derivation provides a microscopic basis for the fractional kinetic equations governed by the Caputo derivative. An exact analytical solution is obtained, yielding closed-form expressions for the time evolution of the state populations. To the best of our knowledge, a time-driven Monte Carlo algorithm is developed for the first time to simulate the irreversible underlying non-Markovian stochastic dynamics governed by a system of Caputo fractional differential equations. The proposed framework is applied to the conformational dynamics of the TbQSOX enzyme, whose relaxation exhibits power-law behavior. The fractional model accurately reproduces the experimental kinetics, providing an estimate of the fractional order $\alpha = 0.22$, which is consistent with the observed anomalous dynamics.

papers.title: A new arrangement inequality (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: We study the cyclic inequality \[ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\,\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^a x_{i+1}^b\;\le\;\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{(1+a+b)/2}\Big)^2, \] where $x_1,\dots,x_n\ge 0$ and indices are taken modulo $n$. Let $N(a,b)$ be the largest $n$ for which the inequality holds for all nonnegative $x_i$. We show that $N(a,b)$ is bounded above by an explicit quantity $N^*(a,b)$ obtained from the second variation at the constant vector, and we conjecture that $N(a,b)=N^*(a,b)$. For $a=b=1$ we prove that the inequality holds if and only if $n\le 8$, which settles the case left open in the original version of this paper. For $n=4$ the inequality holds whenever $1,a,b$ are the sides of a triangle, with an explicit remainder term. We show that $N$ is monotone along rays emanating from the line $a+b=1$; this corrects and extends an earlier monotonicity statement. Finally, any $n$ nonnegative numbers can be arranged so that the inequality holds; for $n\neq 6$ this is achieved by one of $n-1$ prescribed arrangements, which yields a volume bound for every such $n$.

papers.title: A Proof of the Langberg-M\'edard Conjecture
papers.authors: Sirui Liu, Zongpeng Li, Baochun Li
papers.abstract: In communication networks, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, achieving transmission rates unattainable by routing alone in many multicast settings. In multiple unicast, where each source sends a message only to its prescribed destination, the precise capability boundary between coding and fractional routing has long remained unresolved. In this context, the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture asserts that if all sources in a directed network transmit independent messages at a common rate and every destination can recover all source messages by network coding, then replacing every arc by an undirected edge of equal capacity yields a network in which fractional routing can simultaneously deliver each source's message to its prescribed destination at the same common rate. We prove the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture for any number of source-destination pairs and arbitrary network topology. More generally, for an undirected network with a given source set and a disjoint set of allowed destinations, we establish a necessary and sufficient cut-capacity condition for simultaneous unit-rate fractional routing under every assignment of an allowed destination to each source. Networks satisfying the hypothesis of the Langberg-M\'edard conjecture necessarily satisfy this cut condition, so the conjecture follows as a direct corollary.

papers.title: Improved Global Boundedness Criteria via Refined Bootstrap Estimates for a Quasilinear Chemotaxis-May-Nowak System
papers.authors: Xueli Bai, Fang Li, Suying Liu, Xuxuan Luo
papers.abstract: We study a quasilinear chemotaxis--May--Nowak system with nonlinear diffusion growing at least as $s^{m-1}$ at high densities and derive improved criteria for global existence and uniform boundedness. For the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic system, we establish global boundedness when $m>3-\frac{4}{n}$ for $n\in\{2,3\}$ and when $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. For the fully parabolic system, the same conclusion holds under $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. The proof relies on two refined estimates. Weighted space--time control of the nonlinear infection source yields the low-order $L^q$-bounds for the free virus density needed to initiate the bootstrap in the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic case. Subsequently, preserving the product structure of this source in the interpolation argument allows the chemotactic contribution to be absorbed more efficiently by the nonlinear diffusion. These estimates improve the previously known sufficient conditions for global boundedness.

papers.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
papers.authors: Paul Bourgade, Pierre Le Doussal, Gregory Schehr
papers.abstract: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/\beta$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $\beta=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

papers.title: Global Boundedness and Finite-Time Blow-up for a Quasilinear Chemotaxis--May--Nowak System
papers.authors: Xueli Bai, Fang Li, Suying Liu
papers.abstract: This paper continues the work of Bai, Li, Liu and Luo \cite{BaiLiLiuLuoPreprint} on a quasilinear chemotaxis--May--Nowak system. We establish global boundedness in three dimensions for both the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic and fully parabolic systems when $m>4/3$. For the former, we construct finite-time blow-up solutions in balls when $n=3$ and $1<m\le4/3$, and when $n\ge4$ and $0<m\le2-2/n$.

papers.title: Representation type of contraction algebras
papers.abstract: We classify the representation-finite, tame, and wild contraction algebras arising from 3-fold flopping contractions of isolated cDV singularities with at worst Gorenstein terminal sources. To achieve this, we first determine the representation type of all contracted preprojective algebras of Dynkin types $\mathsf{A}$, $\mathsf{D}$, and $\mathsf{E}$, and then use the representation type invariance under iterated flops and the radical structure of contraction algebras.

papers.title: Which posets are spectra of Noetherian rings? The case of height at most one
papers.abstract: A finite poset is the prime spectrum of a Noetherian ring exactly when it has no chain of three elements, that is, it is the poset of a finite bipartite graph. This answers Conjecture 5.3 of Alkass. The substance is a construction: minimal elements become curves y=g_i(x), maximal elements points, edges the incidences, arranged by interpolation. The coordinate ring of the union of the curves, localized at the chosen points, is essentially of finite type over Q and of dimension at most one. Dropping finiteness costs two conditions, both isolated by Colbert: a poset with no chain of three elements is a Noetherian spectrum exactly when it has finitely many minimal elements and any two distinct ones have finitely many common upper bounds. A variant keeping the shape of the ideals of Alkass but changing their exponents shows why that construction produces only nested neighborhoods. Constraining the ring destroys most of this freedom: normal rings leave finite disjoint unions of stars, domains a single star, local rings a point or a finite co-star. In height two the question is open in general, but the conditions conjectured by Wiegand and Wiegand are not sufficient

papers.title: Extremal diagonal-coherent binary codes: shortened Hamming cores, deep holes, and the 64 I-Ching hexagrams
papers.abstract: Each of the 64 hexagrams of the I-Ching, or Book of Changes, is a stack of six Yin-Yang lines and is therefore a binary vector of length 6; the eight hexagrams formed by repeating a single trigram span a doubled-trigram subspace $\Delta$. We ask which binary $[6,3,3]$ codes are compatible with this trigram structure. We show that a $[6,3,3]$ code meets $\Delta$ in at most four codewords, that the four are then forced to be the doubled trigrams Earth, Fire, Wind and Lake, and that exactly two codes attain this bound: the shortened Hamming code $\mathcal C_A$ and its dual. Since $\mathcal C_A$ has covering radius 2, its eight codewords, their radius-one balls, and its eight deep holes together reconstruct all 64 hexagrams. In general, we call a binary code of length $2m$ with $d \ge 3$ diagonal-coherent if it contains the half of the diagonal subspace $\{(u,u)\}$ coming from even-weight vectors $u$ -- the largest part of that subspace a single-error-correcting code can contain -- and extremal if its dimension is as large as possible. For $m\ge2$ and $r=\lceil\log_2(2m+1)\rceil$, we determine the number $N(m)$ of extremal diagonal-coherent codes with parameters $[\,2m,\ 2m-r,\ \ge3\,]$, show that diagonal coherence entails no loss of redundancy, and determine their minimum distances. We also put these codes in a normal form, determine their hulls, and show that each has covering radius $2$ with exactly $2^r-1-2m$ deep-hole cosets. Finally we propose three open problems.

papers.title: The chromatic number of a random graph with $o(n^{3/2})$ edges
papers.authors: Amin Coja-Oghlan, Mikhail Isaev, Mihyun Kang, Pavel Zakharov
papers.abstract: Let $G(n,m)$ be the Erdos-Renyi random graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges and let $\delta>0$. Alon and Krivelevich [Combinatorica 1997] proved that for any sequence $m\leq n^{3/2-\delta}$ there \emph{exists} an integer sequence $q=q(n)$ such that the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals either $q$ or $q+1$ with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$. In this paper, we give an explicit formula for this sequence $q(n)$ and confirm their result under a less restrictive assumption that $m=o(n^{3/2})$. Furthermore, we show that for all but a vanishing proportion of the admissible values of $m$, the chromatic number of $G(n,m)$ equals $q$ with high probability.

papers.title: Pseudospectral phenomena preventing the analyticity sector of a Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup to be ruled by the spectral angle of its generator
papers.abstract: We study elliptic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operators in $L^2$ spaces with respect to invariant measures. These operators have discrete spectra and generate analytic semigroups. The angle defining the analyticity sector of a Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroup is not always equal to the complementary angle of the spectral angle of its generator. In this work, we study the link between these two angles. More specifically, we provide a necessary and sufficient criterion ensuring that they are complementary, and explain how pseudospectral phenomena account for these two angles to fail to be complementary.

papers.title: Sharp Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for $q$-Araki-Woods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Semigroups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the sharp $2$-logarithmic Sobolev inequality for $q$-Araki-Woods Ornstein-Uhlenbeck semigroups with $-1<q<1$ and obtain hypercontractivity along the Gross curve with the optimal coefficient, and determine the exact hypercontractive time for $1<p\le2\le r<\infty$. Reverse hypercontractivity holds in the two separate ranges $0<p<r<1$ and $-\infty<p<r<0$. An explicit counterexample rules out the proposed universal reverse curve across zero. We also obtain the complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality via the intertwining property.

papers.title: Limiting moments of sample covariance matrices from large fold tensor vectors
papers.abstract: We study the moments of sample covariance matrices $M_{n,k,m}$ formed from independent $k$-fold tensor products of $n$-dimensional random vectors. The base vectors have independent and identically distributed centered complex entries with unit variance and finite moments of all orders. For every fixed $p \in \mathbb N_+$, under suitable moment conditions, we obtain an asymptotic formula for $p$th moment as $n, k, m$ tend to infinity with $m/n^k \to c \in (0,\infty)$. There is no restriction on the growth rate of $k$ relative to $n$. We also prove a variance bound and obtain the corresponding almost sure asymptotic formula. The results recover known limiting moments in several regimes. When $k/n$ tends to infinity and the modulus of base vector entry is not constant, we establish the asymptotic growth rate for the $p$th moment of normalized matrices. In this regime, we also provide a lower bound for the growth rate of the largest eigenvalue.

papers.title: Failure of interior $L^p$ estimates for nonlocal elliptic equations with continuous kernels
papers.abstract:
Let $0<\sigma<2$ and $1\leq p<\infty$. We construct a fixed linear nonlocal elliptic operator $L$ and functions $u_m\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ such that \[
  \|u_m\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}+\|Lu_m\|_{L^p(B_2)}\longrightarrow0,
  \qquad
  \liminf_{m\to\infty}\|(-\Delta)^{\sigma/2}u_m\|_{L^p(B_1)}>0. \] The kernel is symmetric in the increment variable, uniformly elliptic, and satisfies the standard bounds on its first two derivatives in that variable. Its dependence on $x$ has a uniform modulus of continuity of order $(\log(1/r))^{-1/2}$ as $r\downarrow0$. Moreover, $\|Du_m\|_{L^p(B_4)}\to0$ for $\sigma>1$, and these norms remain bounded for $\sigma=1$. Thus the interior $L^p$ estimates for translation-invariant operators do not extend to this class under mere continuity in $x$.

papers.title: On the isomorphism problem of Cayley digraphs
papers.abstract: A finite group $G$ is called a DCI-group provided any two Cayley digraphs $Cay(G,S)$ and $Cay(G,T)$ are isomorphic iff the two connection sets $S$ and $T$ are images of each other via automorphisms of the group $G$. Building on the vast literature on CI- and DCI-groups we present an updated list of possible DCI-groups. In addition, we give an alternative proof that does not rely on deep results from group theory. We also point out the three most important open problems related to the classification of DCI-groups.

papers.title: Noninteger completely monotonic degrees of Stirling remainders and their derivatives
papers.abstract: For Stirling expansions truncated after at least two Bernoulli terms, we disprove the three real-degree conjectures recorded by Mahmoud and Qi for the signed remainders of the logarithm of the gamma function and their derivatives. We give a unified proof of the corresponding integer-degree formula, recovering known cases and resolving Zhu's conjectures for higher derivatives in this range. Every real completely monotonic degree lies strictly between the predicted integer and the next integer. We obtain a universal fractional lower bound through an explicit inverse function and a simpler rational bound valid for every derivative order. A local estimate for the negative part of the Laplace kernel's derivative with respect to its logarithmic variable makes the lower improvement proportional to the reciprocal of the combined truncation and derivative order. Together with a uniform upper bound, this determines the exact order of decay of the fractional excess for each fixed derivative order and for its supremum over all derivative orders. Sharper kernel estimates give stronger bounds for the first two degrees. The proof combines fractional positivity criteria, the classical Laplace representation, a sign characterization of the associated densities, and a convexity obstruction at the upper integer endpoint. All estimates used in the proofs are analytic. The exact real degrees and the optimal asymptotic constants remain open.

papers.title: Finite-Time Blow-Up for Wave Equations with Nonlinear \(p\)-Laplacian Damping
papers.abstract: We consider a wave equation with linear elasticity, nonlinear \(p\)-Laplacian damping acting on the velocity, and a focusing power source in a bounded three-dimensional domain. For \(2<p<r+1\leq6\), we prove finite-time blow-up in the natural energy norm for initial data in \(H_0^1(\Omega)\times L^2(\Omega)\) lying in the unstable potential well below its depth. This includes every nonzero initial state with nonpositive total energy and requires no sign condition on the initial displacement--velocity pairing. For positive initial energy, we establish a sufficient condition for finite-time blow-up involving the \(L^2\) pairing of the initial velocity with a fixed approximation of the initial displacement. The proof combines a shifted displacement multiplier, an auxiliary quantity built from the time integral of the spatial \(L^p\)-norm of the velocity gradient, and a weighted auxiliary functional. Linking the weight parameter to the initial value of the cumulative quantity allows us to absorb the mixed terms in the auxiliary functional estimate. Together with the shifted displacement multiplier, this yields upper bounds for the maximal existence time in both ranges \(2<p\leq3\) and \(p>3\), without assuming \(W_0^{1,p}(\Omega)\) regularity of the initial displacement.

papers.title: On optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent reward
papers.abstract: In this paper we consider optimal stopping problems with full information and rank-dependent rewards. Our focus is on the following two problems: selecting one of the r best observations (Gusein-Zade's problem with full information) and minimizing the expected rank (Robbins' problem). In both settings we provide full characterization of the optimal stopping rules and corresponding optimal values. We also present numerical experiments in which the derived dynamic programming recursions are implemented, and approximations to optimal values are computed.

papers.title: Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: We study existence and uniqueness of solutions to the vertex-weighted Dirichlet problem on locally finite graphs. Let $B$ be a subset of the vertices of a connected graph $G$. The Dirichlet problem asks for a function whose discrete Laplacian is prescribed on $V\setminus B$ and whose values are prescribed on $B$. Each infinite connected component of $G\setminus B$ is called an end of $G$ relative to $B$. On finite graphs we show that the solution is the limit of an averaging process, with an explicit geometric rate given by the spectrum of the random walk, and is also the limit of the heat flow and the minimizer of an energy functional. On infinite graphs we prove two existence theorems: one with no assumption on vertex degrees, under a finite-width condition and summable data, and one for bounded data on graphs of bounded degree, where the solution is also unique among bounded functions. If there are no ends, the Dirichlet problem has exactly one solution. If there are $l$ ends, the solution set, when nonempty, has dimension at least $l$; each end carries a positive harmonic function vanishing on $B$. Calling an end parabolic when the random walk started in it hits $B$ almost surely, we show that this function can be taken bounded exactly on non-parabolic ends and is necessarily unbounded on parabolic ones, a discrete analogue of a theorem of Li and Tam. Consequently, bounded solutions are unique if and only if every end is parabolic.

papers.title: Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any $S_{\mathcal P}$ with $\mathcal P$ finite.

papers.title: A Necessary and Sufficient Condition for the Existence of Global Smooth Solutions to the One-Dimensional Inviscid Burgers-Vlasov System
papers.abstract: We investigate global smooth solvability for the one-dimensional inviscid Burgers-Vlasov system. For a smooth initial fluid velocity and a nonnegative, compactly supported particle distribution, we establish a sharp necessary and sufficient threshold expressed through the sum of the initial velocity gradient and the initial particle density. The principal difficulty is to control simultaneously the nonlinear steepening of the fluid velocity, the drag coupling, the particle velocity support, and the full hierarchy of derivatives. To overcome it, we introduce a combined gradient-density quantity whose evolution closes along fluid characteristics. Its sign invariance, together with characteristic support estimates and fixed-order derivative bounds, yields global continuation whenever the initial threshold is nonnegative. If the threshold fails at one point, a Riccati comparison gives an explicit finite upper bound for the maximal smooth lifespan and identifies negative velocity-gradient blow-up when this bound is attained. We also use nonnegative regularization and compactness to extend the threshold result to initial data of any fixed finite regularity.

papers.title: Compactness of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a complete characterization of the compactness of arbitrary finite linear combinations of composition operators acting on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. In particular, we obtain a characterization of compactness for linear combinations satisfying the CNC. As an application, we give an affirmative answer to a conjecture raised by Choe et al. [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B 9(2022), 733--756] concerning such Hardy spaces. Furthermore, we establish the phenomenon of (double) difference cancellation for linear combinations of composition operators by constructing explicit examples.

papers.title: Multi-marginal optimal transport on sub-Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study multi-marginal optimal transport on ideal sub-Riemannian manifolds. We establish a sub-Riemannian barycentric balance condition and prove the existence of a solution to the Monge problem under an additional assumption. We also investigate the absolute continuity of Wasserstein barycenters. Our results extend and improve upon those of Pass, Pinamonti, and Vedovato (Methods Appl. Anal. 28 (2021), 61-76) on the Heisenberg group, answering two open questions raised in their work.

papers.title: Movable Curves and Ample Normal Bundles
papers.abstract: We prove that the movable cone of a smooth complex projective variety is the closed cone generated by possibly singular curves with ample coherent normal sheaves, answering a question of Boucksom--Demailly--P\u{a}un--Peternell. For smooth curves, we establish the analogous equality in several geometric settings and give explicit constructions on blowups.

papers.title: Learning Representative Port Subsets for Efficient Fluid Antenna Systems
papers.abstract: Fluid antenna systems (FASs) provide many candidate ports, but probing all ports for each channel realization incurs substantial online overhead. We study a complementary offline problem: compress the candidate-port space once and reuse the compressed set across future channel realizations. The method collects optimal ports from sampled training realizations, requiring only one scan of the candidate ports per realization. On a DeepMIMO 7-by-7 FAS with 49 candidate ports, 120 training realizations yield 27 representative ports on average while retaining 99.995% of the channel power gain achieved by exhaustive port selection.

papers.title: On the power of adaption and randomization 2: Non-symmetric convex sets
papers.authors: David Krieg, Erich Novak, Mario Ullrich
papers.abstract: Let $S:X\to Y$ be a bounded linear operator between real Banach spaces, and let $F\subset X$ be nonempty, bounded and convex. We prove $$a_{2n-1}(S,F)\le 27n\min \{ e^{\rm ran}_n (S,F), e^{\rm ada}_n (S,F)\}.$$ Here $a_k$ is the minimal worst-case error of continuous affine algorithms of rank at most $k$, and $e_n^{\rm ran}$ and $e_n^{\rm ada}$ are the minimal errors of adaptive randomized and deterministic algorithms using at most $n$ continuous linear measurements. This shows that the gain of adaption and randomization, and even nonlinearity, is limited by a factor $27n$ for approximation in convex sets. We discuss the optimality of the result by examples.

papers.title: On the positive Lebesgue measure of (n,k,t)-sets
papers.abstract: We study sets in R^n that contain a unit k-dimensional disk in each direction from a subset of the Grassmannian G(n,k) of Hausdorff dimension at least t; we call them (n,k,t)-sets. In the range 2k>n, we prove that every (n,k,t)-set has positive Lebesgue measure whenever t>k(n-k-1)+1. This follows from a sharp Sobolev-to-L^2 estimate for the k-plane maximal operator over a Frostman measure on G(n,k), which also yields an L^p-L^2 estimate for every p>n/k with respect to Haar measure. In the range 2k<=n, where translations can no longer be ignored, we obtain the same threshold via a lifting argument, conditional on the quantitative Kakeya estimate in dimension n-k+1. Using the quantitative Kakeya estimate of Wang and Zahl in dimension 3, we deduce that (4,2,t)-sets have positive measure for t>3. The threshold t>k(n-k-1)+1 is sharp, in the sense that (n,k,t)-sets of measure zero exist at t=k(n-k-1)+1. These results improve the previous threshold t>n/2+k(n-k-1) of Fraser, Harris and Kroon, and give the first restricted-direction results in the range 2k<=n.

papers.title: Brauer--Manin obstruction for Weil restrictions
papers.abstract: For a quasi-projective variety $X$ defined over a number field $k$, let $X'$ be its Weil restriction with respect to a finite field extension $k/k'$. We prove that the Brauer--Manin set of $X$ agrees with the Brauer--Manin set of $X'$. We also prove the agreement for Brauer--Manin set of them given by $\mathrm{Br}_1$.

papers.title: Partial Information Decomposition When Some Sources Are Known: A Source Chain Rule and a No-Go Theorem
papers.abstract: Partial information decomposition (PID) splits the information that several sources carry about a target into atoms, distinguished by which collections of sources give access to them. We ask how such a decomposition should behave when some of the sources are already known. The access structure of the atoms suggests one answer: discard the atoms that the known sources provide and regroup the rest according to which further sources unlock them. The classical construction of conditional information suggests another: recompute the decomposition under the conditional distributions and average. We show that the two answers agree, atom by atom, exactly when redundant information obeys a source chain rule, an analogue of the chain rule of mutual information: when the same sources are added to several collections, the enlarged collections share everything the added sources provide and, beyond that, exactly what the original collections share once the added sources are known. The rule divides established measures of redundant information, so that adopting or rejecting it genuinely narrows the choice of measure. Our main result is a no-go theorem: for three or more sources, the source chain rule and local positivity, the requirement that all atoms be nonnegative, cannot hold together in any PID.

papers.title: A Bestiary of Brownian Processes: A Field Guide to Boundary Conditions and Conditioning
papers.abstract: The covariance of Brownian motion is the Green kernel of the one-dimensional Laplacian with a pinned left endpoint and a free right endpoint. This correspondence between Green's functions for the Laplacian on an interval and Brownian covariance functions turns out to be a general phenomenon. We use this correspondence to organize Brownian-derived Gaussian processes by three operations: choosing a self-adjoint realization, recentering a path, and conditioning a fixed law. Local Robin and selected nonlocal boundary conditions yield a catalogue of twelve processes with closed-form kernels, Brownian-path constructions, spectra and traces. The periodic and Neumann-Neumann realizations annihilate the constants; projecting the source and imposing zero time average selects the corresponding covariance pseudoinverses. Recentering and conditioning can both give a Brownian path zero time average, but the resulting laws differ: a constraint alone does not specify a process. A rank-one conditioning identity gives a scale-invariant criterion for the covariance effect of a shrinking family of observations. For Brownian finite differences of any fixed positive order, the covariance effect vanishes uniformly as the spacing tends to zero. For $m$-fold integrated Brownian motion, derivative constraints of orders $1,\ldots,m$ remain detectable at interior times. For simulation, we identify which grid constructions are exact and which are approximate.

papers.title: When Protection Hurts: A Cytokine Storm Theory of Supply Chain Overreaction
