  We also prove that quadratic Teichm\"uller curves are characterized by the existence of a holomorphic splitting of the logarithmic cotangent Kodaira-Spencer map. This result is the analogue of M\"oller and Viehweg's characterization of Kobayashi geodesics in $\mathcal A_g$.

papers.title: Convex orders in root systems and quantum tangent spaces
papers.authors: Alessandro Carotenuto, Christophe Hohlweg, Paolo Papi
papers.abstract: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.

papers.title: Number of equations defining the Kummer varieties of hyperelliptic curves
papers.abstract: The Jacobian of an hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is equipped with a symmetric theta divisor $\Theta$ that defines a principal polarization. The line bundle $\mathcal{O}(2\Theta)$ defines an embedding of the Kummer variety $K$ inside the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$, which factorizes inside a certain orthogonal Grassmannian. We describe a minimal free resolution of $K$ inside this Grassmannian using geometric representation theory. As a consequence, we obtain a formula for the number of quartic equations defining $K$ in the projective space $\mathbb{P}^{2^g-1}$.

papers.title: New families of additive non-RS MDS codes and ACD codes from twisted Reed-Solomon codes
papers.authors: Xia Li, Yu Wang, Yansheng Wu
papers.abstract: Additive codes generalize linear codes and play an important role in the construc?tion of quantum codes. As generalizations of linear MDS codes, additive MDS codes have received much research attention. As an important subclass of additive codes, ACD codes are widely used for quantum error correction. In this paper, we study single-twist additive generalized twisted Reed-Solomon (GTRS) codes over finite fields. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for these codes to be MDS for arbitrary hook and twist parameters. Then we employ Schur squares to prove that such additive MDS codes are not monomially equivalent to additive Reed-Solomon codes. We also identify a class of additive GTRS codes whose duals remain additive GTRS codes, and show that, for all sufficiently large prime powers q whose characteristic avoids a finite set, such GTRS codes yield ACD codes.

papers.title: On a family of stably handle-slide trivial R-links
papers.abstract: An R-link is an n-component link L in S^3 such that Dehn surgery on L yields #^nS1 \times S2. Adapting work of Gompf, Scharlemann and Thompson, Meier and Zupan produced a family of R-links L(p, q; c/d), where the pairs (p, q) and (c, d) are relatively prime and c is even. For most of link in this family, whether it is handle-slide trivial remains open. In this work, we show one subfamily, L(3, 2; 4/d), are stably handle-slide trivial for all d.

papers.title: Universal polynomials for Gromov-Witten invariants on toric surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the polynomiality of combined logarithmic and ordinary Gromov-Witten invariants with a Lambda class insertion on toric surfaces $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$. We show that the combined logarithmic Gromov-Witten invariants can be expressed in terms of universal relative node polynomials when the direction vector $\mathbf{c}$ and length vector $\mathbf{d}$ of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ are sufficiently large and spread out. In particular, when the normal fan of the $h$-transverse lattice polygon $\Delta(\mathbf{c},\mathbf{d})$ is smooth and its edges satisfy a length condition, we show that the combined Gromov-Witten invariants are equal to a universal node polynomial. We also show that the higher genus Block-G\"ottsche polynomials of smooth toric surfaces corresponding to these $h$-transverse lattice polygons, including toric blowups beyond Hirzebruch and toric del Pezzo surfaces, are equal to a generating function of higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants.

papers.title: Deformations of the logarithmic tangent bundle of smooth projective surfaces
papers.abstract: We study fixed-determinant deformations of the logarithmic tangent bundle associated with a smooth irreducible divisor on a smooth complex projective surface. We derive numerical criteria for the existence of positive-dimensional deformation families. Using the Enriques--Kodaira classification and Miyaoka-type inequalities, we classify the minimal surface pairs whose logarithmic tangent bundle is infinitesimally rigid. We also prove monotonicity under compatible blow-ups and compute local comparison formulas for resolutions of low-multiplicity ordinary singularities of the boundary.

papers.title: Smooth stationary water waves with multiple vortex spikes
papers.authors: Zhiqiang Fan, Yuchen Wang, Youquan Zheng
papers.abstract: For any prescribed positive integer $n$, we establish the existence of a family of stationary solutions to the two dimensional capillary-gravity water wave equations in finite depth, whose stream functions exhibit $n$ well-separated vertically aligned vortex spikes with alternating signs. The construction is based on a nonlinear gluing scheme for a singularly perturbed semilinear elliptic equation coupled to the Bernoulli equation on the free surface. Our results extend the single-spike construction to arbitrary finite multi-spike configurations and reveal a mechanism through which exponentially localized vortex spikes can coexist with an almost flat free surface.

papers.title: Non-local Interfacial Energies in Grain Boundaries via Dirichlet-to-Neumann Map and Energetic scaling
papers.abstract: This paper deals with the variational analysis of edge dislocations arising in small-angle grain boundaries (Read--Shockley) and semi-coherent interfaces (van der Merwe). Using the Nabarro--Peierls approach to model edge dislocations, we reduce the two-dimensional isotropic Navier--Lam\'e system governing the linearized elastic energy to a one-dimensional non-local energy on the slip interface through a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. We prove that the resulting boundary energy coincides, up to a multiplicative constant, with the fractional \(H^{\frac12}\)-Gagliardo seminorm of the displacement jump along the interface. Within this framework, we establish the existence of a unique global minimizer by combining our dimensional-reduction result with the characterization of De Luca, Goldman, and Ponsiglione. Indeed, we show that the optimal defect configuration is uniquely attained, up to translations, by an equispaced periodic array. Finally, we provide a physical rescaling that recovers the classical logarithmic energy regimes of both the Read--Shockley and van der Merwe models.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Graph-Codes Avoiding Complete Bipartite Differences
papers.abstract:
Let $d_{K_{s,t}}(n)$ be the largest fraction of all graphs on $[n]$ in a family containing no two distinct members whose symmetric difference is a copy of $K_{s,t}$. We determine this maximum density for every fixed pair of positive integers $s,t$. If both part sizes are odd, it is known that the density is exactly $1/2$. Otherwise, let $2h$ be the largest even part size. We prove $$ d_{K_{s,t}}(n)=\Theta_{s,t}(n^{-h}). $$ For $h>1$, this improves the general $O_{s,t}(1/n)$ upper bound obtained from Alon's two-copy gluing theorem~\cite{Alon2024}. The sharp bounds for even stars were already proved by Alon and are recovered as special cases.
  The upper bound uses the Frankl--F\"uredi forbidden-intersection theorem. For the lower bound, we construct binary linear codes using BCH codes. When exactly one part size is even, we assign to each edge the sum of the binary vectors assigned to its endpoints. When both part sizes are even, we identify these vectors with elements of a finite field and assign to each edge the product of its endpoint elements. In both cases, every copy of $K_{s,t}$ has a nonzero syndrome.

papers.title: Weighted density bounds for covering systems over Dedekind domains
papers.abstract:
We study the density of uncovered sets arising from finite families of residue classes over Dedekind domains with finite residue norms. Building on the distortion method of Balister, Bollob\'as, Morris, Sahasrabudhe and Tiba, we prove a general weighted density criterion in which the weight attached to a prime ideal is allowed to vary. In the critical Mertens regime this yields, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the admissible prime-ideal weight \[
  1+\frac{(\log N\mathfrak p)^3(\log\log N\mathfrak p)^{1+\varepsilon}}{N\mathfrak p}, \] up to a harmless modification at finitely many small prime ideals. This is asymptotically smaller than the fixed weight \(1+(\log N\mathfrak p)^{3+\varepsilon}/N\mathfrak p\) appearing in the earlier density theorem. The result is valid for systems of any fixed multiplicity and, for multiplicity one, requires the ideal moduli themselves to be distinct but not their norms.
  We then place the analytic hypotheses in Knopfmacher's Axiom~A framework. In the critical case of Axiom~A with exponent \(1\), the prime-ideal estimates needed by the weighted theorem are automatic. More generally, under Axiom~A with exponent \(\rho>0\), we prove a weighted mean-value theorem on ideals; in the subcritical range \(0<\rho<1\), a first-moment argument shows that sufficiently large moduli cover an arbitrarily small proportion of the ambient space. We also explain that the distortion construction itself only uses a compatible system of finite residue spaces with uniform fibres and a Chinese-remainder-type product structure, suggesting a possible extension beyond Dedekind domains. Finally, we show that a direct passage from the second moment to higher integer moments does not lower the logarithmic exponent \(3\) within this moment hierarchy.

papers.title: From Fairness to Efficiency in Repeated Bilateral Trade
papers.authors: Fran\c{c}ois Bachoc (LPP, IUF), Tommaso R Cesari (uOttawa), Roberto Colomboni
papers.abstract: Recently, Bachoc et al. (2026) proposed an axiomatic approach to fairness for repeated bilateral trade. Their resulting objective is a H\''older mean of seller and buyer utilities with non-positive order $\lambda$, interpolating between Rawlsian fairness at $\lambda = -\infty$ and Nash fairness at $\lambda = 0$. Here we study this family of H\''older means in the complementary setting of orders $\lambda \in (0,1]$, which constitutes a tradeoff between fairness and efficiency, with the weight of efficiency increasing with $\lambda$, and where $\lambda=1$ yields the existing gain from trade criterion, focusing solely on efficiency. We obtain an axiomatic characterization of these H\''older means, relying on a Pigou-Dalton principle of transferring from rich to poor. From an online learning perspective, we show that, contrary to the case $\lambda \le 0$, the problem is unlearnable in full generality, even under seller's and buyer's valuation independence. We focus on seller's and buyer's valuations with distributions having bounded densities, in which case we obtain matching lower and upper bounds on the cumulative regret, of order $\widetilde{\Theta}(T^{2/3})$ with respect to the time horizon $T$. The upper bounds rely on a reconstruction identity where the expected objective is written as a gain-from-trade term plus a two-dimensional integral involving the seller and buyer distribution and survival functions, and a kernel function. For $0 < \lambda < 1/2$, the strong singularity of the kernel is addressed by two main ingredients. First, we propose a new zooming algorithm that sequentially rejects or refines layers of the set of prices. Second, we propose a tailored decomposition of the two-dimensional integral, enabling us to truncate it with a controlled impact on the truncation error. For $1/2 \le \lambda \le 1$, the singularity of the kernel is mild enough, so that the existing scouting bandit algorithm, already proposed for the case $\lambda=1$, can be extended.

papers.title: Zero temperature versus long time for diffusions driven by metric projections onto convex sets
papers.abstract: For a closed subset $C$ of Euclidean space, we study the diffusion whose drift pulls the state towards its nearest point in $C$, with noise intensity $T$. We let $T$ tend to zero and time tend to infinity. Convexity of $C$ is equivalent to a pathwise bound of the distance from $C$ by the norm of the process of Ornstein and Uhlenbeck. For arbitrary closed sets the bound holds in law. For compact convex $C$, we describe the invariant law by the curvature measures and the intrinsic volumes of $C$. The limit points of the law of the state form the orbit of reflected Brownian motion in $C$ started from the projection of the initial law. So the two limits commute only when this projection is the uniform law on $C$. Unless $C$ is a point, the mixing time is of order $1/T$ up to a logarithm. For the control problem the two limits of the value function commute for every compact convex set and every bounded Lipschitz terminal cost. A companion paper treats finite disjoint unions of convex sets.

papers.title: Singular Limits of Frame Bundles of Noncollapsing Positively Curved Manifolds
papers.abstract: For each dimension $n\ge 2$, we construct noncollapsing sequences of metrics on $S^n$ with a uniform positive lower bound on sectional curvature whose oriented orthonormal frame bundles, equipped with the canonically induced connection metrics, converge to nonmanifold metric spaces homeomorphic to $\Sigma(S^{n-1}\times\SO(n))$. In even dimensions, real projective quotients give connected full frame bundles with the same limits, disproving the manifold conclusion in Yamaguchi's frame bundle conjecture. In odd dimensions, each component of the full projective frame bundle, with its intrinsic metric, converges to the quotient of the spherical limit by a free involution. The singularities are detected by local homology, and we obtain quantitative equivariant Gromov--Hausdorff estimates. We also compare the frame bundle limits with the intrinsic completions of their regular limiting frame metrics, and present and discuss alternatives to Yamaguchi's original conjecture.

papers.title: Structure-preserving discretisations for the quasi-incompressible, thermal Maxwell-Stefan equations
papers.authors: Boris D. Andrews, Aaron Baier-Reinio, Aaron Brunk, Patrick E. Farrell, M\'aria Luk\'a\v{c}ov\'a-Medvi\v{d}ov\'a
papers.abstract: We study a thermal Maxwell-Stefan-Navier-Stokes system modelling miscible mixtures under a quasi-incompressibility constraint. The system consists of the conservation laws for mass and momentum, and the balance law for entropy, which is preferred over the balance law for energy because it facilitates the development of two structure-preserving discretisation methods. The first method applies a semi-implicit Euler scheme in time, together with suitable finite elements in space, which guarantees generation of entropy and enforces the quasi-incompressibility constraint pointwise, but numerically dissipates total energy. The second method employs a continuous Petrov-Galerkin discretisation in time, which also generates entropy and satisfies the constraint pointwise, and in addition conserves the total energy and allows high-order time approximations. The structure-preserving properties and behaviour of both numerical methods are demonstrated by a series of numerical experiments.

papers.title: Bounds on the number of squares in recurrence sequences: $y_{0}=b^{2}$ (II)
papers.abstract: For binary recurrence sequences, $\left( y_{k} \right)_{k \in \bbZ}$, arising from the solutions of generalised Pell equations, $X^{2}-dY^{2}=c$, where $y_{0}$ is any positive square and $c=-2^{\ell}p^{m}$ for an odd prime $p$ and non-negative integers $\ell$ and $m$, we show that there are at most $4$ distinct squares with $y_{k}$ sufficiently large. From this result, we also show that there are at most $7$ distinct squares when $y_{0}=1,2^{2},\ldots,7^{2}$, or once $d$ exceeds an explicit lower bound, without any conditions on the size of such squares.

papers.title: Regularized Sequential Reconstructions of Dynamic Nonsmooth Sources from Sparse Boundary Flux Data
papers.authors: Davide Bianchi, Tianrui Dai, Hongqin Zhang, Shupeng Zhang, Zhidong Zhang
papers.abstract: We consider an inverse source problem for the heat equation on the unit disk $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ with flux measurements at finitely many boundary points. The source is piecewise constant in time on prescribed intervals and, on each interval, is the characteristic function of an unknown region with Lipschitz boundary. The measurements on each interval split into the contribution of the current source and a history term from earlier sources; subtracting the latter leaves a linear inverse problem for a forward operator $F_\tau$ that is densely defined and unbounded on $L^2(\Omega)$. We prove that $F_\tau$ is not closable, so the classical regularization theory for closed unbounded operators does not apply. We regularize instead with a Hilbert-scale penalty that compactifies it. The resulting Galerkin--Tikhonov reconstruction is sequential: each source is recovered from the flux observed up to the end of its interval and from the previously reconstructed sources. We prove its convergence and uniqueness, show that earlier reconstruction errors propagate into later data with exponential decay in time, and establish stability estimates with respect to the number of sensors. A numerical experiment on noisy measurements shows the feasibility of the sequential approximations, refined by Fourier approximation and boundary correction by a neural network.

papers.title: The modular characters of $\text{Sp}_{10}(2)$
papers.abstract: Using computational methods, we determine the irreducible $3$- and $5$-modular characters of the symplectic group $\text{Sp}_{10}(2)$ for blocks with non cyclic defect groups, with one ambiguity in the principal $3$-block.

papers.title: Global regularity for a class of degenerate/singular Monge-Ampere equations
papers.authors: Fan Cui (School of Mathematics Science, Tianjin Normal University, Tianjin, China), Huaiyu Jian (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing, China, Department of Mathematical Sciences, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China), You Li (School of Mathematics and Computational Science, Xiangtan University, Hunan, China), Yannan Liu (School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing, China)
papers.abstract: We study the global regularity of solutions to the homogeneous Dirichlet problem for a class of Monge-Ampere equations, which become degenerate or singular on the boundary due to the zero boundary value and the distance function. The degeneracy and singularity are described by the index - the sum of the powers of the distance function and the solution. We give a complete classification of the index, and prove that the solution is globally Holder continuous, log-Lipschitz continuous, $C^{1,eta}$, $C^{2,alpha}$ and $W^{2,p}$ respectively, depending on the size of the index. We also obtain estimates related to the five regularity results. All these results are optimal.

papers.title: General Relativity for Mathematicians - Part I
papers.abstract: These notes cover the first part of a course of the same title taught by Filippo Fila-Robattino and Manuel Tecchiolli at the University of Zurich in the Winter Semester of 2025. Topics include variational principles in classical mechanics, special relativity, smooth manifolds and tensor calculus, connections and curvature, geodesic motion, and the derivation of Einstein's equations from the Einstein-Hilbert action. The treatment is aimed at a mathematical audience, combining physical motivation with precise definitions, detailed proofs, and explicit calculations.

papers.title: Global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ Convergence of Multilevel Gradient-Regularized Newton Methods
papers.abstract: We develop and analyze multilevel gradient-regularized Newton methods for unconstrained convex optimization with Lipschitz-continuous Hessians. By computing Newton corrections in lower-dimensional subspaces, the proposed methods aim to reduce computational costs while preserving the global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ convergence rate in function values of the full-space method. To establish this rate for multilevel methods, we introduce a class of row-nested restriction operators that ensures monotonicity of the reduced-gradient norms across levels. Numerical experiments with row-nested operators demonstrate convergence behavior comparable to full-space gradient-regularized Newton, while offering substantial computational savings on large-scale instances.

papers.title: Non-discrete complex hyperbolic $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$-triangle groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study complex hyperbolic triangle groups of type $(p_1,p_2,p_3;p_4)$ with $3\le p_1\le p_2\le p_3\le p_4\le \infty$. We show that if the element $R_1R_2R_3$ is elliptic, then the group is either non-discrete or it belongs to a short list of known discrete groups.

papers.title: Structural taxonomy and complex irreducible representations of non-abelian groups of order p^4
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $G$ be a non-abelian group of order $p^4$. The classification of groups of order $p^4$ provides a natural setting for studying the structure of their complex group algebras. In this paper, we consider a non-abelian group G of order $p^4$ and determine the primitive central idempotents of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}G$. Using these idempotents, we obtain the corresponding decomposition of $\mathbb{C}G$ into simple components and describe the irreducible representations of $G$. The results provide an explicit description of the representation-theoretic structure of the chosen non-abelian group of order $p^4$ and illustrate the role of primitive central idempotents in the Wedderburn decomposition of its complex group algebra.

papers.title: Uniqueness and attractiveness of stationary solutions in a harvesting mean field game
papers.authors: Greta Lamonaca (IDP, CEREMADE, UO), Idriss Mazari (CEREMADE), Gr{\'e}goire Nadin (IDP, CNRS)
papers.abstract: Sustainable harvesting of natural resources is a central challenge both in ecology and economics. This paper explores a MFG model for harvesting in an aquatic ecosystem. Such systems have recently attracted attention from the applied mathematics community, and, due to the interplay between the competition of agents and the internal dynamics of the fish population, the analytical properties of the resulting system are very delicate to study. In the present work, we focus on stationary solutions, with a strong emphasis on their uniqueness and dynamical stability.

papers.title: A PDE-Based Model of Runner Flow in Mass Participation Events
papers.authors: Alice Molinari, Brian Block, Stephanie Stockar, Simona Sacone
papers.abstract: This paper presents a macroscopic approach for modeling pedestrian movement. A convection-diffusion partial differential equation (PDE) is described and used to model the flow of runners along a marathon course. A marathon is a good modeling case study for human movement because the location of runners is only known in sparse locations, so an accurate model is needed to know where people are at all times. As well, marathons offer many safety and logistical problems that can be solved by modeling human movement. Data is obtained from the 2023 Columbus Marathon, and model improvements are made to include a temporally varying convection term. Results show an increase in model accuracy which can allow for better resource allocation and safety measures.

papers.title: Falconer estimate for circular and cinematic Furstenberg problem
papers.abstract: We prove the Falconer-type bound $\dim_{\mathrm H}F\geq u+1$ for planar circular $(u,v)$-Furstenberg sets whenever $0<u\leq1$, $0<v\leq3$, and $2u+v\geq3$. The same bound holds for smooth cinematic curve families. This resolves the circular Furstenberg conjecture of Green, Harris, Ou, Ren, and Tammen in its full Falconer range $2u+v\geq3$.

papers.title: On the symmetric Morrey problem in three dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the relations between seven generalized notions of convexity for continuous integrands in the space of symmetric $3\times 3$ matrices. Here, symmetric quasiconvexity is defined through symmetrized gradients, and symmetric rank-one convexity through symmetrized rank-one lines. We construct a symmetric quasiconvex integrand that is not polyconvex at symmetric matrices, and an integrand that is both symmetric rank-one convex and Hessian quasiconvex but not symmetric quasiconvex. We also establish a transfer principle that converts smooth rank-one convex functions that lack Hessian quasiconvexity into symmetric rank-one convex integrands while preserving this lack of of Hessian quasiconvexity. Applying this scheme to already existing counterexamples yields the existence of symmetric rank-one convex integrands that are not Hessian quasiconvex. Together with known examples, these results determine all pairwise implications among the seven notions considered here.

papers.title: Large deviations for observables with logarithmic singularity and differentiability of the pressure function
papers.abstract: We show that logarithmic observables of form $\phi(x)=\log(|x-b|)$ on the doubling map $T$ have exponential large deviations with respect to the invariant measure if $b$ is preperiodic but not periodic with respect to $T$ giving a counterpart to the known result of strictly stretched exponential large deviations in the case that $b$ is periodic. These results are established by showing that the topological pressure function developed for unbounded observables is differentiable at $0$.

papers.title: The flipping principle for boundedly acyclic covers and colorings
papers.authors: Pietro Capovilla, Alberto Casali, Marco Moraschini
papers.abstract: Based on the theory of multicomplexes and other ideas by Gromov, we describe the flipping principle. This is an easy geometric criterion that forces the vanishing of the Gromov norm of homology classes. We use it to provide proofs based on a common geometric principle of the Vanishing Theorem and the Amenable Reduction Lemma by Gromov in the case of amenable and boundedly acyclic covers and colorings. We also strengthen the conclusion of the Amenable Reduction Lemma by showing that it implies the $\ell^1$-invisibility of the homology classes and not only the vanishing of their Gromov norm.

papers.title: Optimal $K_t$-free list colorings and the Pollyanna property of graphs with no triangular wheel
papers.abstract: A wheel consists of an induced cycle of length at least four and a vertex with at least three neighbors on the cycle. Let $\cal T$ be the class of graphs with no wheel containing a triangle. We prove that, for every $G\in\cal T$ and every integer $t\ge3$, the $K_t$-free chromatic and choice numbers both equal $\lceil{\omega(G)/(t-1)}\rceil$. We further prove that $\cal T$ is $k$-strongly linear-Pollyanna for every integer $k\ge2$, and hence is linear-Pollyanna. In particular, the class of wheel-free graphs is Pollyanna, answering Problem 10.2 of Chudnovsky, Cook, Davies and Oum.

papers.title: A cohomology operation encoding the octahedral axiom
papers.abstract: We introduce a new secondary cohomology operation, the naturality defect product, associated with a graded natural transformation between the cohomology functors of two differential graded functors, and study its main properties. We then prove that a pretriangulated category satisfies the octahedral axiom if and only if the naturality defect product associated with the natural isomorphism given by a theorem of Heller vanishes on the homotopy category of acyclic complexes over it. This characterization extends immediately to n-angulated categories. As an application, we exhibit non-vanishing instances for the recently found examples of pretriangulated categories which are not triangulated. Finally, we show that horizontal composition of these natural isomorphisms preserves n-angulated structures, and we use it to obtain, from each of these examples and for every r >= 1, a pre-3r-angulated category which is not 3r-angulated.

papers.title: Continuity of the phase transition for long-range Bernoulli percolation with exponential decay on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$
papers.authors: Omer Angel, Daniel de la Riva, Christoforos Panagiotis, Yuliang Shi
papers.abstract: We prove continuity of the phase transition for long-range Bernoulli percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^{2}$ with connection probabilities that decay at least exponentially fast. This extends earlier work by Duminil-Copin, Sidoravicius, and Tassion on slabs. Our proof establishes a finite-size criterion that allows us to run a renormalisation argument. As a corollary, we obtain supercritical sharpness, in the sense that for every $\beta>\beta_c$, there exists a unique macroscopic cluster in large boxes with high probability.

papers.title: Combinatorial decompositions of strict partitions and multi-sum Rogers-Ramanujan type identities
papers.abstract: While multi-sum Rogers-Ramanujan type identities have been extensively investigated through Bailey pairs, the constant term method, complex contour integration, and related techniques, many still lack an intrinsic combinatorial understanding. In this paper, we establish combinatorial interpretations for several families of triple-sum identities via structural decompositions of strict partitions. For one of these families, we extend the underlying combinatorial framework to obtain a general $(m+1)$-fold multi-sum identity. Leveraging these partition-theoretic interpretations, we construct explicit bijective proofs for all the corresponding identities. As an application, this constructive approach naturally yields some parameterized generalizations.

papers.title: Uniqueness of the maximal function field with the third largest genus in characteristic $3$
papers.authors: Peter Beelen, Maria Montanucci, Jonathan Niemann
papers.abstract: Let $n$ be a positive integer and define $q=3^n$. It is well known that there exists a maximal function field $Z_3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3=q(q-1)/6$ and that $g_3$ is the third largest genus a maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ can have. In this article we show that any maximal function field over $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$ of genus $g_3$ is isomorphic to $Z_3$. This extends previously known uniqueness result for the largest and second largest genera of maximal curves.

papers.title: The Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence can be arbitrarily non-degenerate in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: There is a long tradition of constructing smooth projective varieties in positive characteristic with non-degenerate Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequences. In this paper, we show that for any $n\geq 1$ and any spot $(i, j)$ on the $E_n$-page, except for the cases where the differential is forced to be zero for trivial reasons, there exists a smooth projective variety whose Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence has a non-zero differential with source $E_n^{i, j}$. Our construction is inspired by constructions of nilmanifolds in complex geometry and can be regarded as a positive characteristic analogue.

papers.title: Bach-flat metrics and global regularity of conformal structures
papers.authors: Rodrigo Avalos, Albachiara Cogo, Andoni Royo Abrego
papers.abstract: We study global regularity properties of conformal structures on compact manifolds with applications to conformally invariant variational problems. We find sharp conditions ensuring that a manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric of Sobolev class is conformally diffeomorphic to a smooth one. In particular, we prove that $W^{2,q}$ Bach-flat four-manifolds with $q > 2$ are smooth up to conformal diffeomorphisms. We also solve the Yamabe problem for $W^{2,q}$ metrics with $q > 2$ on three-manifolds under a mild conformal condition.

papers.title: A non-perturbative topological persistence theorem for normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds
papers.abstract: Floer proved that, under a sufficiently small $C^0$ perturbation, a normally hyperbolic invariant manifold gives rise to a nearby invariant set whose cohomology ring contains a subring isomorphic to that of the original manifold. Using topological conditions, expressed in terms of the so-called covering relations, we generalize this theorem to a non-perturbative context. Our result does not require the existence of an invariant manifold before perturbation, nor does it require the original map to be smooth or invertible. For the proof, we develop an additional structure on the Conley index for maps on vector bundles.

papers.title: The Serre closure of Banach spaces
papers.authors: F\'elix Cabello S\'anchez, Jes\'us M. F. Castillo, Ra\'ul Mart\'inez-Boh\'orquez, Jos\'e Navarro Garmendia
papers.abstract:
We determine the Serre closure of Banach spaces in the category of quasi-Banach spaces, that is, the smallest class of quasi-Banach spaces that contains all Banach spaces and is stable under subspaces, quotients, and extensions. Precisely, a quasi-Banach space $X$ belongs to this closure if and only if there exist constants $M$ and $k\in\mathbb N$ such that $$ \frac{\|x_1+\dots+x_n\|}{\|x_1\|+\dots+\|x_n\|}\leq M\log^k n $$ for every $n\geq 2$ and every $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$; equivalently, $X$ is a quotient of an Orlicz sequence space $\ell(I,f_l)$, where $I$ is an index set and $f_l(t)$ is equivalent to $t\log^l(1/t)$ near zero.
  The proof combines geometrical estimates for quasi-Banach spaces and quasilinear maps with the study of higher order derived spaces associated to complex interpolation between $\ell_{2/3}$ and $\ell_2$. We provide examples of spaces in the Serre closure of Banach spaces that are not iterated extensions of Banach spaces and discuss some related problems.

papers.title: Liouville Theorems for the Stationary Fractional Hall-Magnetohydrodynamic Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove Liouville-type theorems for the stationary fractional Hall-magnetohydrodynamic equations in $\mathbb R^3$. Smooth solutions vanishing at infinity, with $u\in\dot H^{\alpha/2}$ and $b\in\dot H^{\beta/2}$, are trivial for $1\le\alpha\le\frac53$, $1\le\beta<2$ and $\alpha+2\beta\le5$, with no additional integrability assumption. The key step is to estimate the Hall boundary term through the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension of $b$.

papers.title: On AI and Progress in Mathematics: Dreaming a Mathematical Universal Machine
papers.abstract: In the autumn of 2026, mathematics is facing what may be the deepest crisis in its history. The entire ecosystem through which mathematical knowledge is produced, validated, communicated, and assessed is beginning to break down. Mathematics departments, those usually quiet and civilized places, are suddenly in turmoil -- the unlikely theaters of a new Battle of the Ancients and the Moderns. The source of the crisis is clear: AI systems have become better than even the best human mathematicians at proving and validating mathematical results. This document proposes a metaphor for mathematical activity: we once thought of ourselves as mountain climbers; soon, we may become miners digging in the mathematical mine, either collaborating or competing with mathematical AI machines. Publications would then be seen primarily as a means of helping humans understand mathematics, while the measurement of mathematical progress would be entrusted to a Mathematical Universal Machine. In nontechnical terms, we explore what this brave new world of mathematics might look like and how we might collectively shape its future.

papers.title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.

papers.title: Regular Graphs Without Isomorphic Bisections
papers.abstract: A graph is bisectable if its vertex set can be split into two sets inducing isomorphic subgraphs. Ando conjectured that every cubic graph is bisectable, and Das, Pokrovskiy, and Sudakov proved it for large enough connected cubic graphs. We give a constructive proof that, for every $d\geq5$, there exists a non-bisectable $d$-regular graph of even order.

papers.title: New thoughts on fractional Sobolev spaces
papers.authors: Angha Agarwal, Pekka Koskela, Khanh Nguyen
papers.abstract: We introduce the concept of a fractional upper gradient and employ it to characterize the $p$-Muckenhoupt weighted $s$-fractional $p$-Sobolev spaces on $\mathbb R^d$ where $d\in\mathbb N$, $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$.

papers.title: On a question of Cid-Ruiz: positive results and counterexamples
papers.authors: T. H. Freitas, V. H. Jorge P\'erez
papers.abstract: In this paper we give positive criteria and counterexamples to a question of Cid-Ruiz on whether intrinsic polar multiplicities detect reductions of modules. Over an excellent regular local surface with infinite residue field, we compute the entire polar sequence of every finite-colength submodule of a free module, showing that its only variable entry is the order of the determinant ideal. This computation yields classes for which equality of polar multiplicities characterizes reduction, while also producing counterexamples in every positive rank, including integrally closed modules with identical intrinsic Hilbert functions and arbitrarily large relative Buchsbaum--Rim multiplicity. In arbitrary dimension, we prove that, under equidimensionality and a sharp dimension bound on the kernel of the induced map of associated graded Rees algebras, equality of the sums of the polar multiplicities characterizes reduction.

papers.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for 2D $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ lattice gauge theory at all couplings
papers.abstract: We prove that the log-Sobolev inequality holds for the two-dimensional $SU(N)$ Wilson lattice Yang--Mills measure with arbitrary fixed inverse coupling $\beta$. The log-Sobolev constant depends on $\beta$ and $N$, but is uniform in the volume of the underlying lattice. The proof relies on a two-scale disintegration argument.

papers.title: Scott-type inequalities for trinomial $h^*$-polynomials
papers.abstract:
Motivated by Scott's inequality for lattice polygons, we study normalized volume bounds for lattice polytopes $\mathcal{P}$ with $h^*$-polynomials $1+at^k+bt^\ell$, where $a,b\ge1$ and $1\le k<\ell$. For $\ell>2k$, the coefficients satisfy $a+1\le b$, and consequently ${\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le2b$. In the complementary range $k<\ell\le2k$, we establish the dimension-independent bound \[
  {\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le(2b+1)(k+\ell). \] On the boundary $\ell=2k$ with $b\ge2$, the sharper Scott-type inequality ${\rm vol}(\mathcal{P})\le4k(b+1)$ holds, confirming a conjecture of Higashitani, Nill, and the author. Equality holds if and only if $k=1$ and $a=3b+3$. Moreover, when $\ell=2k$ and $k,b\ge2$, we obtain an upper bound depending only on $b$.

papers.title: The norm reveals projections in the positive unit sphere of an arbitrary C*-algebra
papers.abstract: We show how a simple metric condition in terms of the C$^*$-norm of an arbitrary C$^*$-algebra $A$ can be employed to determine those norm-one positive elements which are projections. Concretely, if we write $S_{A^+}$ for the intersection of the positive cone and the unit sphere of $A$, we establish that an element $a \in S_{A^+}$ is a projection if, and only if, $$\{a\} = \left\{x\in S_{A^+}: \|x-z\| = 1 \hbox{ for all } z\in S_{A^+}\hbox{ with } \|a-z\|=1 \right\}.$$ This proves a conjecture which has been previously confirmed for von Neumann algebras and unital C$^*$-algebras. In the setting of not necessarily unital JB$^*$-algebras, the Shirshov--Cohn theorem is invoked to obtain a similar metric characterisation of projections. In the wider setting of JB$^*$-triples, we show how a metric characterisation in terms of inner ideals can be established to determine non-zero tripotents.

papers.title: Congruences modulo powers of $7$ for partitions with colored odd parts
papers.authors: Saikat Maity, Manjil P. Saikia, Prabal Talukdar
papers.abstract: Let $a_k(n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ in which even parts occur in one color and odd parts may occur in $k$ colors. We prove infinite families of congruences modulo powers of $7$ for $a_k(n)$ when $k \in \{4,5,7\}$. For each positive integer $\alpha$, let $\lambda_{k,\alpha}$ be the least nonnegative solution of $24\lambda_{k,\alpha}\equiv-(k-2)\pmod{7^\alpha}$. Then, we show that \[ a_k(7^\alpha n+\lambda_{k,\alpha}) \equiv 0\pmod{7^{\lfloor(\alpha+1)/2\rfloor}} \] for every nonnegative integer $n$. These results extend congruences modulo $7$ of Hirschhorn and Sellers (2026) and complement Chen's (2025) congruences for the reciprocal crank parity function $a_3(n)$.

papers.title: A Numerical Method for the Fractional Semilinear Calder\'on Problem
papers.authors: Mukul Dwivedi, Jesse Railo, Andreas Rupp
papers.abstract: We present a finite element method for reconstructing a coefficient in a fractional semilinear equation from a single exterior measurement.

papers.title: A theoretically exact filtered back-propagationformula for single-time wave inversion
papers.abstract: We consider single-time wave inversion, that is, recovering the initial pressure $f$ from the wave field $\mathcal{W}_T f = u(\cdot,T)$ at a single time $T$, where $u$ solves the wave equation with sound speed $c$ and initial data $(f,0)$. In two dimensions this is the main reconstruction step of full-field photoacoustic projection imaging, where each camera image is a two-dimensional wave field at a single time instant. An efficient direct method is back-propagation by the Fourier multiplier $2\cos(cT|\xi|)$. It yields exact inversion in odd dimensions but not in two. We give its error in closed form, with bounds, and derive an exact explicit filtered back-propagation $f = 2\mathcal{W}_T \mathcal{M}_K \mathcal{W}_T f$ in analogy to filtered backprojection for the Radon transform.

papers.title: Knot Floer complexes of generalized L-space knots
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study height 4 knots, which generalize L-space knots and almost L-space knots studied by Ozsv\'ath--Szab\'o, Baldwin--Sivek, and Binns. A knot $K\subset S^3$ is called a height $m$ knot if $\operatorname{rank} \widehat{HF}(S^3_n(K))-n=m$ for all integers $n\geq 2g(K)-1$, where $\widehat{HF}$ is the hat version of Heegaard Floer homology introduced by Ozsv\'ath--Szab\'o. In particular, height 0 and height 2 knots are exactly L-space knots and almost L-space knots, respectively. We prove that the knot Floer complex $CFK^\infty(S^3,K)$ of a height 4 knot $K$ admits a basis that is horizontally and vertically simplified--an hv-basis for short. Moreover, we show that under such an hv-basis, the horizontal and vertical differentials fall into six cases, generalizing the results for L-space knots and almost L-space knots. The hv-basis of the knot Floer complex of $K$ can determine, via an explicit algorithm, the immersed curve of Hanselman-Rasmussen-Watson for the knot complement of $K$. Consequently, our results facilitate further exploration of computations of $\widehat{HF}$ for the gluing of two height 4 knot complements.

papers.title: Spectral zeta functions in positive characteristic
papers.abstract:
Spectral zeta functions and zeta-regularized determinants encode the spectrum of an operator in analytic functions. Over the completion $\mathbb C_\infty$ of an algebraic closure of $\mathbb F_q((\pi))$, two features of characteristic $p$ break this classical picture. Complex powers have exponents that vary only continuously in $\mathbb Z_p$, not analytically. Scalar traces record eigenvalue multiplicities only modulo $p$. We develop a resolvent-based theory that treats these two obstructions separately.
  For the first, inverse Stieltjes duality turns suitable scalar resolvents into locally analytic spectral distributions on $\mathbb F_q[[\pi]]$. A single exponent of the Mellin transform already determines the distribution and the entire Mellin family. We characterize exactly which power series arise in this way, by a growth condition on Carlitz moments. The criterion depends on the support: bounded Taylor coefficients are not sufficient. For stationary digit measures, the transform is the unique fixed point of an explicit contraction. The first $q-1$ nonconstant moments recover the measure.
  For the second, we replace traces by the Frobenius defect $F/\sigma(F)$, where $\sigma$ raises coefficients to their $q$th powers. On power series with small coefficients, this map is a group automorphism that preserves Gauss distances, and a convergent infinite product inverts it. Polynomial defects produce entire functions. They characterize exactly the diagonal spectra that are finite unions of forward Frobenius orbits, counted with multiplicity. For the shifted Carlitz operator, the resulting Fredholm determinant is a normalized reciprocal of the Anderson--Thakur function, and its Newton polygon is determined exactly.

papers.title: Quantitative Analysis of Second-Harmonic Generation in Plasmonic Nanowires: Symmetry Breaking and a Topological Defect
papers.authors: Qi Lei, Hongyu Liu, Zhi-Qiang Miao, Guang-Hui Zheng
papers.abstract: This paper develops a quantitative theory of second-harmonic generation (SHG) in hollow plasmonic nanowires, distinguishing geometric symmetry breaking from cavity effects. We consider a centrosymmetric material with a concentric circular cavity and a slightly perturbed outer boundary. Relative to the solid nanowire in~\cite{liu2026quantitative}, the cavity introduces a topological defect by changing the cross-section from a disk to a doubly connected domain, whereas the outer-boundary perturbation breaks geometric symmetry. Local inversion-symmetry breaking at the interfaces induces nonlinear surface polarization. Using layer potentials and boundary-perturbation asymptotics, we derive explicit leading- and first-order formulas for the fundamental and second-harmonic fields. For a circular outer boundary, the leading-order second-harmonic field is purely quadrupolar; its amplitude differs from the solid-wire case by $O(\gamma^2)$ as $\gamma=r_i/r_e\to0$ and decays as $O(r_e-r_i)$ in the nonresonant thin-shell limit. For perturbations proportional to $\cos(n\theta)$, $n\ge3$, the first-order second-harmonic correction contains only modes $n-2$, $n$, and $n+2$, yielding dipolar, quadrupolar, or higher-order radiation for $n=3$, $n=4$, or $n\ge5$, respectively, provided the lowest-order modal coefficient is nonzero. We derive plasmonic resonance conditions at both frequencies and estimate the singular orders of single and simultaneous resonances, including possible higher-order singularities from coincident resonance factors. Thus geometric symmetry determines the multipolar modes, whereas the cavity radius controls their amplitudes and resonant enhancement.

papers.title: Quadratic Returns for a Moving Water Tank: An Explicit Right Inverse and a Sylvester Representation
papers.abstract: Coron's return method established local nonlinear controllability of a moving water tank in sufficiently large time. We study the quadratic response at uniform equilibrium, where the acceleration input in the linearized model cannot excite the Fourier modes of the fluid with even indices. At three one-way wave crossings (T=3), we construct a nonzero smooth acceleration, whose first two final-state coefficients vanish. A planar curve reduces this cancellation to a scalar identity. At this reference acceleration, two integrations give an explicit control correction that preserves the linear return and produces any given leading change in the quadratic final state. The correction maps periodic $H^r$ targets with zero mean to $H^r$ controls for every nonnegative integer $r$. A contraction argument also gives local exact solvability of the quadratic final-state equation. Finally, a time-dependent Sylvester equation provides an alternative representation of the coupling responsible for the second-order correction. The associated change of state coordinates involves one spatial derivative, while the control correction preserves regularity in appropriate Sobolev spaces. These results concern the first two variation equations and not yet the fully nonlinear model.

papers.title: Uniform Exponential Stability for Finite Energy Weak Solutions to the Barotropic Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations with Large Potential External Forces
papers.abstract: We study the large-time behavior of Lions--Feireisl finite energy weak solutions to the barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations in three-dimensional bounded domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions and large potential external forces. For $\gamma>3/2$, we prove that these weak solutions converge exponentially to the steady state as time tends to infinity, provided that the steady density is bounded away from zero. The main novelty of our analysis is a compactness argument based on Young measures. Furthermore, we prove that the Young measures generated by the density are Dirac measures. Together with the extra integrability of the density, this yields strong convergence to the nonconstant steady density and uniform smallness of the energy $w$ for sufficiently large time. We use Taylor expansion and the Bogovskii operator to construct a Lyapunov functional, and use this smallness of $w$ to obtain exponential decay with a time $T_0$, which is independent of the particular weak solution, thereby answering the question raised by Kang, Peng and Xiong in \cite[Remark~1.1]{KPX}. Corresponding decay estimates for the density, momentum, kinetic energy and the viscous dissipation integrated from large times to infinity also hold, allowing vacuum.

papers.title: Maximum length and size of simultaneous core partitions with distinct parts
papers.abstract: We give, for the first time, a formula for the largest size of an $(s,t)$-core partition with distinct parts valid for every coprime pair. We also determine the greatest number of parts of an $(s,t)$-core partition whose successive parts differ by at least $D$, whenever $\gcd(s,t)\le D$, removing the restrictions on the core parameters in the formula of Burson, Sisneros-Thiry, and Straub. The size formula uses a column description and a single Dedekind sum. The length formula uses coefficients from the Euclidean algorithm and satisfies a recurrence in smaller core parameters. We construct partitions attaining each maximum.

papers.title: Comparing and measuring intermediate tail dependence
papers.abstract: The tail dependence function $\Lambda$ of a bivariate copula, and the tail dependence order based on it, cannot distinguish between copulas whose tail dependence coefficient vanishes; for all of them $\Lambda\equiv 0$. Such copulas, among them the Gaussian copulas with correlation $\rho<1$ and the lower tails of all extreme-value copulas other than the comonotonicity copula, are nevertheless ordered by the much finer information contained in their tail expansion $C(u w)\sim u^{\kappa}\ell(u)\,b(w)$, where $\kappa$ is the tail order, $\ell$ is slowly varying and $b$ is the tail order function of Hua and Joe. We introduce an asymptotic tail order $\preceq$ that refines the tail dependence order and show that it is lexicographic in the three quantities $\kappa$, $\ell$ and $b$. As a consequence, every real-valued measure that is monotone with respect to $\preceq$ is constant on all but countably many tail-order classes; meaningful measures of intermediate tail dependence must therefore be defined level-wise, and we construct such measures. Finally we determine where the fine structure resides: if the joint tail is ray-regular on the exponential scale, then $b$ is determined by the tail order and the one-sided derivatives at $\omega=1/2$ of the angular dependence function of Wadsworth and Tawn; it is a (possibly broken) product of powers. If the joint tail is log-concave on the exponential scale, $b$ is squeezed between two such products.

papers.title: Self-consistent flow maps based on commutator-free exponential integrators
papers.abstract: We develop a flow-map framework for nonlinear transport equations, comprising a self-consistent exact frozen flow and its numerical realization. An exponential--pullback identity represents each frozen transport exponential in a commutator-free exponential integrator as the pullback induced by its exact backward characteristic map. Composing these maps defines the self-consistent exact frozen flow, a time-discrete construction with autonomous frozen fields formed from linear combinations of transport fields evaluated at the stage approximations. A local freezing-error identity and a one-step estimate for the Lie--Euler Vlasov--Poisson update separate field variation, field approximation, and characteristic integration errors; these estimates do not assert global PDE convergence. We specialize this construction to the Vlasov--Poisson system and obtain the self-consistent numerical flow through velocity-space quadrature, a discrete Poisson solve, field interpolation, and numerical integration of the frozen characteristic equations. Under suitable regularity assumptions, we prove that the self-consistent exact frozen flow for this system is a volume-preserving diffeomorphism. Temporal self-convergence tests on Vlasov--Poisson and guiding-center benchmarks yield rates consistent with the design orders and illustrate conservation behavior and the evolution of solution structures in long-time simulations with large time steps.

papers.title: On the asymptotic behaviour of $\alpha$-divergence generalized posteriors
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the solutions to the unconstrained generalized variational inference problem regularized by an $\alpha$-divergence. Under mild conditions, the minimizer is explicit up to a scalar normalizing constant, and we show that it admits a rescaling under which it converges in $L^1$ to a fixed non-Gaussian law, at a concentration scale around the empirical loss minimizer that departs from the typical $n^{-1/2}$ in the classical Bernstein--von Mises theorem. For $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $d<2/(1-\alpha)$ the limit is a Student-$t$ distribution and the posterior width shrinks faster than the sampling error of the empirical minimizer. Conversely, for $\alpha>1$ the limiting distribution is a compactly supported Pearson type-II distribution, and the posterior width shrinks more slowly than the sampling error. The KL divergence ($\alpha=1$) is the unique member of the $\alpha$-divergence family whose posterior width matches the sampling scale and whose limit is Gaussian. We discuss the implications of these qualitatively different regimes for the frequentist coverage of credible regions, and a toy example on intercept-only logistic regression illustrates the theoretical claims.

papers.title: Measurement-dependent reduction of open dynamics in the quantum phase estimation algorithm: the visible subspace and the damped Fej\'er kernel
papers.authors: Marina O. Gordeichuk, Oleg M. Kiselev
papers.abstract: For the quantum phase estimation (QPE) algorithm we study the minimal space of observables that is sufficient to predict the entire output distribution under open dynamics of the counting register. Building on the general Krylov theory of reduction, we compute the structure of this space explicitly for the full Fourier measurement. The outcome probabilities are determined by cyclic sums of the state matrix. If the adjoint generator is diagonal on the matrix units, the spectral classes inside the residue classes of the index difference modulo the register dimension $M$ give a constructive basis, an exact dimension formula, and attainable bounds: the dimension of the visible space lies between $M$ and $M^2-M+1$. The class includes independent qubit dephasing, and an analytically solvable reference model of Gorini--Kossakowski--Lindblad--Sudarshan (GKLS) type yields a damped Fej\'er kernel; two random-unitary channels with the same Ramsey contrast show that higher harmonics are distinguishable in the QPE distribution. For approximate reduction we use a finite-time Gramian and an a posteriori residual estimate, with a quadratic error order for a reducing unperturbed subspace and a compatible initial state. Numerical calculations check the consistency of the representations and the behaviour of the error under non-Toeplitz perturbations.

papers.title: Revisiting the Schwarz Lemma for the Pentablock: Counterexamples and Sharp Interpolation Criteria
papers.authors: Shubhankar Mandal, Avijit Pal, Bhaskar Paul
papers.abstract: Alshehri and Lykova (\emph{J. Geom. Anal.} \textbf{33} (2023)) formulated a Schwarz lemma for the pentablock $P$, giving a criterion for the existence of an analytic map from the unit disc $\mathbb D$ into the closed pentablock $\overline P$ that sends the origin to the origin and a prescribed point $\lambda_0\in\mathbb D$ to a given point $x_0\in\overline P$. We show that the sufficiency direction of their criterion is false. We identify the underlying error as the extension to the open unit disc of a Fej\'er--Riesz identity that is valid only on the unit circle. We establish a corrected necessary and sufficient interpolation criterion when the last two components are prescribed by a fixed rational $\Gamma$-inner function and resolve the special case $s_0=0$. Using the Poisson integral representation of the associated outer spectral factor, we obtain a sharp comparison between the corrected bound and the bound proposed by Alshehri and Lykova, with a precise characterization of equality. We further express the logarithmic difference between these bounds as a nonnegative Green potential, thereby quantifying the discrepancy in terms of the derivative of the first coordinate of the prescribed $\Gamma$-inner function. Finally, we formulate a variational problem over rational $\Gamma$-inner interpolants satisfying the prescribed two-point conditions. We show that the supremum of the associated outer-factor quantities determines the maximal admissible modulus of the first coordinate among pentablock-valued interpolants whose last two components belong to this class. Equivalently, this extremal problem reduces to minimizing the corresponding Green potential. We conclude by discussing the remaining problem of characterizing unrestricted Schwarz interpolation for the pentablock and its connection with the Lempert function.

papers.title: The monotone part of Chatterjee's rank correlation
papers.abstract: Chatterjee's rank correlation $\xi$ measures how strongly a random variable $Y$ depends functionally on a random variable $X$, but it does not distinguish increasing, decreasing and non-monotone relationships. We ask how much of the dependence measured by $\xi$ is explained by an increasing relationship. For continuous marginals, $\xi$ is, up to a factor, a squared distance from independence in a Hilbert space geometry derived from the Sobolev scalar product for copulas. We answer it by the metric projection onto the closed convex set of stochastically increasing copulas in this geometry. The projection is explicit: it replaces every vertical section by its least concave majorant, and it coincides with the smallest stochastically increasing copula dominating the given one. It splits $\xi$ orthogonally into a monotone part $\xi^{\uparrow}$ and the squared distance to the class of stochastically increasing copulas; dually, $\xi^{\uparrow}$ is, up to a factor, the squared distance to the polar cone, which corresponds to negative quadrant dependence. The monotone part vanishes exactly for negatively quadrant dependent copulas, equals $\xi$ exactly for stochastically increasing copulas, and equals one only for the comonotonicity copula. In contrast to $\xi$, it is increasing in the concordance order and continuous with respect to weak convergence. Symmetrisation decomposes the measure of mutual complete dependence in the same way. Finally, the construction extends to arbitrary distributions via isotonic regression of conditional distribution functions. In particular, the plug-in estimator based on the empirical distribution is strongly consistent for every copula, without smoothing or tuning parameters.

papers.title: A Robust ADI-Based Direct Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Two-Dimensional Singularly Perturbed Parabolic PDEs
papers.abstract: This study proposes two-dimensional one-parameter singularly perturbed parabolic problems and develops an operator-splitting direct discontinuous Galerkin (DDG) method for their numerical solution. To improve computational efficiency, an alternating direction implicit (ADI) splitting approach decomposes the original two-dimensional problem into two separate one-dimensional subproblems. The spatial discretization is performed using the DDG method on a piecewise-uniform Shishkin mesh, enabling accurate resolution of the sharp boundary layers that arise in singularly perturbed problems (SPPs). For the temporal discretization is carried out with the backward Euler scheme to ensure robustness and stability. The theoretical analysis establishes an optimal convergence rate of order $k$ in the spatial discretization, where $k$ denotes the degree of the polynomial basis functions, and $(\Delta t)$-order convergence in temporal dimensions. We prove that the resulting fully discrete scheme is consistent, stable, and convergent. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Further Study of p-Ary Self-Orthogonal Codes From Square Functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate a family of trace codes over finite fields of odd characteristic defined by two quadratic trace conditions. By analyzing the quadratic forms associated with these trace conditions and evaluating the corresponding character sums, we obtain the parameters and complete weight distributions of the codes. We further exploit the natural multiplicative orbit structure of the defining sets to obtain punctured codes and determine their parameters, weight distributions and dual distances. Moreover, we establish self?orthogonality criteria and investigate divisibility and projectivity of the constructed codes. These results give a unified treatment for arbitrary odd prime fields and for extension degrees of both parities.

papers.title: From one particle to N particles: uniform transport-information and log-Sobolev inequalities for Coulomb gases on the torus
papers.authors: A Guillin (LMBP), W Liu (LMBP), B Nectoux (LMBP), L Wu (LMBP)
papers.abstract: We study how a functional inequality satisfied by the one-particle conditional distributions of a Gibbs measure, with a constant independent of the positions of the other particles, can be propagated to the whole N -particle system, with a constant independent of N , when the interaction is singular. Our model is the Coulomb gas on the torus T 3 in the mean-field regime. We distinguish two mechanisms. The first one is a dependent tensorization, governed by Dobrushin-Wu interdependence coefficients. It yields uniform Poincar{\'e} and transport-information W 2 I inequalities with fully explicit constants. We explain why this mechanism does not extend to the log-Sobolev inequality: the Zegarlinski-type coefficients, which require pointwise bounds on the interaction, are infinite. The second mechanism is a tensorization with a defect. Using a uniform bound on the partition function due to Duerinckx and Jabin, it yields a uniform log-Sobolev inequality for the Coulomb gas on T 3 at small charge. We identify the assumptions on the interaction under which each mechanism applies. All the results are then extended to the two-dimensional Coulomb gas and to periodic Riesz gases 1/|x|^s , 0 < s $\le$ 1. The extension to d $\ge$ 4 is also discussed.

papers.title: $RO(G)$-graded cohomology of a point is self-injective
papers.authors: Eric Hogle, Clover May, Foling Zou
papers.abstract: Generalizing known results for $G=C_2$ and constant $\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$-coefficients, we show the $RO(G)$-graded Bredon cohomology of a point with constant $\underline{k}$-coefficients is self-injective whenever $G$ is a finite subgroup of $SO(3)$ and $k$ is a finite field. Self-injectivity holds more generally for the $RO(G)$-graded homotopy of the Eilenberg--MacLane spectrum associated to a $k$-linear commutative Green functor $M$, whenever the spectrum $HM$ is Anderson self-dual.

papers.title: Sharp Fourth-Moment Wasserstein CLT Bounds
papers.authors: Xiao Fang, Zi-Yao Su, Jiaxue Wang, Xiaolin Wang
papers.abstract:
We prove that for the normalized sum $W=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i/\sqrt{n}$ of independent, mean-zero, $d$-dimensional random vectors with $\operatorname{Cov}(W) =\Sigma=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\dots, \sigma_d^2)$ (the diagonal form of the covariance matrix is assumed without loss of generality), the 2-Wasserstein distance from $W$ to $N(0,\Sigma)$ is bounded by \[\sqrt{2\sum_{j=1}^d \min \left\{\sigma_j^2, \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E} [|X_i'-X_i|^2(X'_{ij}-X_{ij})^2 ] }{n^2 \sigma_j^2} \right\}},\] where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm, $X_i'$ is an independent copy of $X_i$, and $X_{ij}$ ($X_{ij}'$ resp.) denotes the $j$th coordinate of the vector $X_i$ ($X_i'$ resp.). On the one hand, it gives the optimal rate $O(\beta\sqrt{d/n})$ if $|X_i|\leq \beta$ for all $i$. On the other hand, in the isotropic case where $\Sigma=I_d$, it gives the optimal fourth-moment bound $O\left(\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}|X_i|^4/n^2}\right)$. Moreover, the coordinatewise minima suggest a tradeoff between the na\"ive coupling and the normal coupling for each component.
  To prove the main result, we develop a new transportation inequality using a coupling via the F\"ollmer process with a general covariance matrix and the martingale property of its drift. The resulting bound is then controlled using a Bonis-type expansion together with Bessel's inequality. The method and the result extend to $p$-Wasserstein bounds. As a consequence, we obtain the Hilbert space 4-Wasserstein CLT bound $O(n^{-1/4}[\operatorname{tr}(Q^{1/2})]^{1/2})$, where, in the i.i.d. case, $Q=\mathbb{E}[|X_1'-X_1|^2(X_1'-X_1)^{\otimes2}]$ and the $O(n^{-1/4})$ rate is optimal given the dimension-free form of $Q$. We further strengthen it to a dimension-free strong approximation result with a near-optimal error rate through the KMT embedding construction.

papers.title: Multilinear extrapolation on Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: We solve an open problem on the multilinear Rubio de Francia extrapolation on Banach function spaces. The first result states that, under the assumption of boundedness of the multisublinear Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, the multivariable boundedness on Banach function spaces can be extrapolated from some weighted Lebesgue space, including the cases where some exponents may be infinite. Under the same assumption, the second result asserts that if a multilinear operator is bounded on some weighted Lebesgue space, then its compactness can be extrapolated from some unweighted Lebesgue space to Banach function spaces. Our results do not require any convexity or concavity conditions on Banach function spaces. The main ingredients in the proof are a multilinear version of the Rubio de Francia algorithm, a stopping-time argument, convex analysis, and a compactness criterion on Banach function spaces. As applications of extrapolation theorems, we obtain multilinear extrapolation for the boundedness and compactness of commutators on Banach function spaces. These results can be further applied to specific operators, which cover both the full range case including multilinear Calder\'{o}n-Zygmund operators, multilinear pseudo-differential operators, and bilinear paraproducts, and the limited range case including the bilinear Hilbert transform, multilinear rough singular integrals, and bilinear oscillatory Fourier multipliers.

papers.title: Ground states for Brezis-Nirenberg-type fractional elliptic systems with sublinear absorption and subcritical perturbation
papers.abstract:
This paper addresses the non-local fractional counterpart of the Laplace equation involving critical nonlinearities, a famous problem originally investigated by Brezis and Nirenberg in [Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 36(4) (1983), pp. 437--477]. We study a class of fractional elliptic systems and equations with critical exponents, sublinear absorption, subcritical perturbation, and general noncoercive frequency parameters. The work is carried out both within a general framework involving non-local integrodifferential operators and in specific concrete models.
  Our results extend and complement the existing literature on critical fractional elliptic problems in several directions: (1) we include sublinear absorption together with a subcritical perturbation, so that the overall nonlinearity is not superlinear at zero; (2) we provide two types of concrete verification of the energy threshold condition in the presence of the critical term, the sublinear absorption, and the subcritical perturbation, whereas the existing verifications are restricted to the pure critical case; (3) we obtain ground state solutions for coupled systems, not merely nontrivial solutions for scalar equations; (4) we allow a general noncoercive range of frequency parameters, including negative values.

papers.title: Encoding Time Series Dynamics with Sliding-Window Signatures for Online Forecasting
papers.authors: Nina Drobac (LPSM), Margaux Br{\'e}g{\`e}re (LPSM), Joseph de Vilmarest (LPSM), Olivier Wintenberger (LPSM)
papers.abstract: Accurate forecasting often relies on both past target values and exogenous variables as inputs. In many applications, however, the time series of interest are non-stationary and the relationship between target and inputs evolves over time, requiring forecasters that adapt online. Moreover, inputs affect the target not only through their current values but also through their recent joint dynamics. We address these challenges in three steps. First, to encode the series dynamics, we rely on signatures of the input paths over sliding windows. Motivated by the universality of linear functionals of signatures, we fit a regularized linear regression on these features to capture nonlinear, path-dependent effects. Second, the simplicity of the linear model allows us to update it online as new data arrives, using a Kalman filter to track dynamic effects. Third, to capture dependencies at several time scales, we combine forecasters built on different window lengths through online aggregation. For French national electricity load forecasting, our method outperforms various state-of-the-art approaches. It also remains competitive across several benchmark datasets with exogenous variables.

papers.title: Initialization Stability and Convergence of Projected Langevin Dynamics
papers.authors: Qi Feng, Nathan Sauldubois, Xin Zhang
papers.abstract: The entropic regularized optimal transport (EOT) plays a fundamental role in the computation of optimal transport. In \cite{CLP}, the authors proposed a gradient flow approach to EOT, and derived a projected Langevin diffusion that converges in distribution to the solution of EOT when initialized with a coupling between the two given marginals. In this paper, motivated by samplings of optimal couplings for EOT, we analyze the projected Langevin dynamics with arbitrary initial distribution, and prove that its long time behavior is the same as if it was initialized from a coupling.

papers.title: Unique direct-sum decompositions of infinite-dimensional unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group via real CMV matrices
papers.abstract:
Unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group arise naturally and play an important role in a wide range of areas including mathematics, physics, and engineering. CMV matrices, introduced by Cantero, Moral, and Vel\'azquez, are five-diagonal unitary matrices that are standard tools in the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. It is known that every unitary representation of the infinite dihedral group on a separable Hilbert space admits a discrete direct-sum decomposition into representations arising from the natural factorizations of real CMV matrices and copies of two exceptional one-dimensional irreducible representations.
  We prove that such a decomposition is unique up to unitary equivalence when the summands arising from real CMV matrices are grouped according to their multiplicities and the spectral measures of the corresponding matrices are mutually singular across distinct multiplicities. Furthermore, we show that the representation associated with each such real CMV matrix $C$ admits a direct integral decomposition into irreducible unitary representations with respect to the push-forward of the restriction of the spectral measure of $C$ to the closed upper half circle.
  These results make it possible to study the structure of unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group using CMV matrices and the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.

papers.title: Minimality of Binary Codes From Weight Layers and Graph Cut Spaces
papers.authors: Xianhong Xie, Mengni Wang, Tingting Wu
papers.abstract: Minimal binary linear codes play an important role in secret-sharing schemes and in the structural study of linear codes. We study the minimality of three classes of known constructions: codes from a single complete Hamming-weight layer, codes from arbitrary unions of such layers and graph cut-space codes. For the previously studied single-layer codes C, we give a complete minimality classification: C is minimal if and only if t is even. For t = 4, we determine the minimum and maximum weights, and show that the family strictly violates the binary Ashikhmin Barg sufficient condition for every k. We also calculate the minimum distance of the dual code. For arbitrary unions of complete Hamming-weight layers, we obtain an if-and-only-if classification of minimality and uniform criteria for evenness, self-orthogonality, the doubly even property and hull dimension. We further analyze the family for odd k. Finally, using the classical bond characterization of cuts, we translate minimality of graph cut space codes into a graph-theoretic condition: a nonempty simple graph has a minimal cut code precisely when it has one edge-containing component and that component is complete. We also give a graph-function realization of the known binary tetrahedron code and explicitly identify the resulting code equivalence.

papers.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
papers.authors: Priyanka Grover, Hemant K. Mishra, Sarishti Singh,  Temjensangba
papers.abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a positive global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a positive local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. Our main tool is a reduction of $s$-principal compression to a rank-$k$ singular value perturbation. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

papers.title: An unconditionally convergent BDF2-type finite element integrator for the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation
papers.authors: Michele Ald\'e, Hywel Normington, Dirk Praetorius, Michele Ruggeri
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete numerical scheme to approximate solutions to the inertial Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (iLLG) equation, a state-of-the-art model to describe the dynamics of the magnetization at subpicosecond time scales. The method employs first-order finite elements for the spatial discretization and the two-step backward differentiation formula (BDF2) for the time discretization, where the inertial term is treated by a convex combination of BDF2 and the backward Euler method. We prove well-posedness and unconditional stability of the scheme, and obtain explicit bounds for the error in the realization of the iLLG-inherent unit length constraint satisfied by the magnetization. Moreover, we derive the discrete energy law satisfied by the approximations, which resembles the inherent dissipative energy law of the model. Finally, with a constructive approach, we prove unconditional convergence of the approximations toward a weak solution of the problem. Numerical experiments assess the performance of the scheme and validate the theoretical findings.

papers.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
papers.abstract: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology.
